projects.title: 放弃 Linear 后，我开发了 Gitstride：一个 GitHub Projects 的 macOS 原生客户端
projects.author: zwyyy456
projects.summary: 我之前半年，开发个人项目的时候一直在用 Linear 来进行项目管理。本来我以为免费配额是够用的，但最近几个月，我同时开发多个项目，Issue 就多了起来，Linear 的免费配额就不够用了，因此，我就转向了 GitHub Projects ，毕竟这些项目的代码本来就托管在 GitHub 上。 迁移到 GitHub Projects 之后，我发现它内置的 PR 与 Issue 联动工作流不如 Linear 完善，也不太符合我的需求。比如，当我给一个 Issue 关联 Draft PR 时，我希望这个 Issue 的状态能自动变成 `In Progress`；当 PR 准备好 Review 的时候，Issue 的状态也能跟着变成 `In review`。如果一个 Issue 关联了多个 PR ，我希望等这些 PR 全部合并之后，它才会进入 `Done`，而不是合并其中一个 PR 就算完成了。 此外，我也不太喜欢每次都要打开网页来管理项目，还是更想用本地客户端来操作。 所以，在 codex 的协助下，我用 Swift 6 开发了 [GitStride]( https://gitstride.hyperseek.tech/zh-cn)，一个 GitHub Projects 的 macOS 原生客户端。 GitStride 实现了前面提到的状态联动规则，我不用再随着 PR 的进度手动修改 Issue 状态。如果 Project 里没有 `In review` 这个状态，设置 GitStride 的 PR 自动化后，GitStride 默认会按需为你自动在 Project 中添加这个状态。 > 设置 PR 自动化时，也可以选择后续不追加 In review 这个状态。 GitStride 在菜单栏会常驻一个图标，点击图标可以快速查看项目 Issue ；等我真的要整理任务时，再打开主窗口，在看板或表格视图中创建和编辑 Issue 。 [![pn1KrPe.png]( https://s41.ax1x.com/2026/09/25/pn1KrPe.png)]( https://imgchr.com/i/pn1KrPe) [![pn1K2rt.png]( https://s41.ax1x.com/2026/09/25/pn1K2rt.png)]( https://imgchr.com/i/pn1K2rt) 为了确保创建 Issue 、更新 Issue 描述等需要向 Github 多次发送请求的操作的跟手，GitStride 开发时借鉴了 Linear 的 local-first 的理念。GitStride 会把项目快照缓存在本机。修改改状态后，界面会先显示变化，再同步到 GitHub ；创建或编辑 Issue 提交后，app 会马上显示新内容，后台处理向 Github 发起的请求。 GitStride 还支持创建 Backlog 状态的 Issue ，新建 Issue 时可以直接选择 Backlog 状态；如果 Project 里没有这个状态，GitStride 会自动补上。 项目已经[开源在 GitHub]( https://github.com/zwyyy456/GitBoard)。如果你也在用 GitHub Projects ，欢迎试试，如果觉得好用，还请给个 Star 。更多介绍，参见 [GitStride 官网]( https://gitstride.hyperseek.tech) 下一步计划 1. 添加命令面板功能、完善 app 内的快捷键操作 2. 添加甘特图视图

projects.title: Show HN: Local Software Factory – running multiple coding agents in parallel
projects.author: gianlucabertell
projects.summary: Hi, as I kept getting confused by having multiple Claude sessions open, last weekend I decided to combine two of my favorite emerging technologies and give it a try: Software Factory and JEV. The idea is simple, inspired by GitHub Actions, I wanted a way to "queue" agent work on my local laptop, with the ability to define different pipelines via YAML. Each pipeline runs in its own Git worktree, so it's isolated from the others. I'm using some pipelines: dev: code → test → commit plan: plan → human review → code → test → commit security: code → human review → test → security review → commit frontend: code → React test → build → commit A request can move up and down the pipeline and be reworked if an agent or JEV flags it! I'm also using JEV to check if a potential secret is leaked, if the coding agent output asks for human review, etc. The real magic happens when you take a single Agent session as the main driver. You can then plan and queue multiple features at once. I think it worked out pretty well, so I open sourced it: https://github.com/stratonext/software-factory You can try it yourself with: uv tool install software-factory Note: You need a JEV key if you want to use the judging steps.

projects.summary: Hello, My name is Kostya Vasilyev and I was the original developer of an Android email app called Aqua Mail, sold to MobiSystems in 2019 at 3.5 organically grown users. After that, I built a new email app called Sugar Mail, based on a cloud email sync platform. The project hasn't been a success with end users, but I think the sync platform could be useful to someone so I'm looking to sell it and include the app too. Mail sync runs in the cloud and supports IMAP and Exchange, both with push mail, and the latter with bi-directional calendar and contact sync. Both Office 365 and on-prem Exchange are supported. Running mail sync in the cloud allows the Android app to be very efficient in terms of battery use. The Android app is just a JSON RPC client with some UI on top - so building an iOS or a desktop app would be pretty easy for the buyer. There are several geo-distributed server nodes and the Android app uses the closest one. Adding nodes for capacity is easy. The project is actively maintaned, with the Android app optimized for Android 17. The server is written in Go. I recently rewrote it in Rust, but decided to stay with Go in production for a variety of reasons (would be happy to explain in more detail). Unit economics: a $10 VPS can handle 1000 users each averaging 2 email accounts. A comparable platform is Nylas which charges $15/month per 10 accounts and has no end-user app (they used to, but not anymore). More details here: https://sugarmail.app/for-sale-one-pager.html Happy to answer questions.

projects.summary: 背景：MiniMax H3 （ 33B 视频生成模型）官方本地推理只支持 CUDA ，Mac 上基本不可用。antirez （ Redis 作者）写了 h3.c —— 纯 C + Metal 的 Apple Silicon 原生推理引擎。 我把它封装成了 ComfyUI 自定义节点并上架了官方 Registry ，应该是 h3.c 生态的第一个 ComfyUI 插件： - 两个节点：文生视频（画幅 / 时长 / 步数 / 速度预设 / seed / 首尾帧）+ Ref2VA 参考生成（最多 9 张有序参考图 + 1 条参考音频） - ComfyUI 界面内实时进度（分阶段进度条）、可取消；标准 VIDEO 输出直接接 SaveVideo - 已经下载过模型权重的话直接把目录指过去就行，不用重下 268GB - 97 个 pytest 用例 + 真机端到端验证（ M 系列 MBP 128G ，512×512 / 4 步约 32 秒） 设计上没有重写任何引擎逻辑，就是 subprocess 包 CLI —— 上游更新 git pull && make 就能获得；包内不含二进制和权重，README 里有完整的构建和模型引导。 Registry： https://registry.comfy.org/nodes/wild-h3c GitHub： https://github.com/skaiy/wild-h3c-comfyui 和官方 MiniMax 节点是互补关系：本地免费快速迭代，定稿后接官方 API 节点出 2K 成片。欢迎试用和反馈。

projects.summary: 最近在 V2EX 看过几个**学英语的产品**了,都不错，有些想法确实很好，等有时间，我也借鉴一下。 接下来，介绍一个精心打磨的学英语网站。**前前后后陆陆续续开发了差不多 10 个月** ![]( https://img.erpweb.eu.org/imgs/2026/09/2c96818200c1ce3b.png) 我始终觉得，一个**好用的工具**，应该具备**好看，简单的特点。**于是最近耐心重新打磨了一下我的**背词背句产品。** 为什么要强调**背词背句**呢，因为实际上**我做了两个网站**，一个强调的是背词背句，主打**一个通过打字学英语**。在打字学英语的基础上，增加一些辅助功能，如：学音标，练习口语（影子跟读）。接入相关评测服务。 而另外**一个负责**提供主动输入**（看视频 听播客）语境视听** 两个的 UI 和 UX 我目前对**背词背句产品**比较满意，因为打磨过的次数版本迭代比较多。后续可能会对产品二进行二次 UI 打磨。 **产品一（背词背句）核心功能**： - 单词练习：敲键盘背单词，默写/不默写都行 - 句子练习：支持连词成句，有句子成分讲解 - 单词计划：允许选择词库计划每天学多少 - 复习系统：采用 FSRS v4 间隔算法 记忆加入系统的单词 - 跟读评测：打分/反馈调整建议 **产品二 (看视频 听播客）核心功能**： - 全英视频：通过 Volg 切片字幕学英语，有标记重点词汇与词汇分类 - 播客混听：内置外接一些播客订阅源（自动处理） - 听力精听：可以一句一句听，有四六级资源 ``` 注册地址： keykey.xin 如果有需要使用 stripe 下单的 可以使用这个地址注册（会贵一点点）功能一样 keykey.im ``` ``` 两个产品采用 sso 互联，一个号两用 产品二从注册地址访问后的侧边栏可以前往 ``` ## 下方码如果领取完了，请留言注册后的用户名 ### 背词背句产品截图： ![]( https://img.erpweb.eu.org/imgs/2026/09/96bc90c18854a661.png) ![]( https://img.erpweb.eu.org/imgs/2026/09/f68c6341b2894b19.png) ![]( https://img.erpweb.eu.org/imgs/2026/09/48597d8dc490dbad.png) ### 产品二 (看视频 听播客）截图： ![]( https://img.erpweb.eu.org/imgs/2026/09/4364a6c53be5aad4.png) ![]( https://img.erpweb.eu.org/imgs/2026/09/33a870469db365a3.png) ![]( https://img.erpweb.eu.org/imgs/2026/09/39852038a0f6ad92.png) 最开始，与一个朋友说我想开发这个产品的时候，朋友第一句话就是说，又不能赚钱，别浪费时间。 但是我总觉得在赚钱之外，有些东西还是需要去做的，感谢自己坚持了快一年。 **目前依旧是在按计划耐心打磨，我是长期主义，虽然目前赚不到什么钱，但是这已经成为了我生活的一部分。经常每天睡醒就有新的想法，这就是我想做东西。也感谢很多给产品体验提供过建议反馈的朋友们，谢谢你们。** ![]( https://img.erpweb.eu.org/imgs/2026/09/d0065573d4d87c09.png)

projects.title: 世界首款基于 jev 的 AI 实时模拟小镇上线了，比斯坦福小镇 200 倍速度，成本减少 90%！
projects.author: Koimiao

github.name: NevaMind-AI/JevTown
github.description: jev based AI town simulation

projects.summary: 最近 jev 的讨论挺多，我们把它接进了「斯坦福小镇」的 agent 模拟世界，做了一个小实验。 虽然它用了像素风游戏的表现形式，但这个世界里没有玩家角色。人类只能观察，不能控制居民。画面中所有会移动的角色，都是 agent 依靠 jev 自己决定要去哪里、找谁，以及什么时候停下来。 目前场景里有 20 个居民。每个人都有自己的身份、性格、当前状态和对世界的共同认知。 世界运行后，他们会不断经历这样一个循环： 观察当前环境 → 决定下一步做什么 → 移动 → 发起互动 → 对话 → 更新状态和记忆 这次主要实验的是：能不能让 jev 来负责 agent 最频繁的「下一步做什么」决策（ repo 里面有录屏） 我们的做法不是让模型自由生成一段 JSON ，而是先由引擎计算出当前合法的候选动作，例如： - 现在可以接近哪些人或物体 - 可以走向哪些地点 - 是否值得主动接触某个目标 - 如果不行动，应该短暂停留还是等待更久 然后把这些候选项交给 Jev 。一次请求里会同时询问 seek 、target 、roam 、place 和 idle_length ，再由代码按照固定规则组合成最终动作。 这样做主要解决了一个之前比较麻烦的问题：普通对话模型即使被要求输出 JSON ，仍然可能选择一个根本不存在、或者当前不可达的目标。Jev 的 Choice 问题只能从引擎提供的候选项里选择，相当于让非法动作从结构上就无法被表达。 同时，它还会返回每个选项的概率和置信度，所以右侧观察面板里可以看到类似这样的记录： seek 0.83 · talk to Ovid p=0.62 c=0.70 这比让模型事后生成一句“我为什么这么做”，更方便观察 Agent 的真实决策过程。 当然，Jev 目前并没有负责整个 Agent 。 它只替换了动作决策这一环。人物对话、长期状态描述和记忆仍然由对话模型与 Embedding 完成。Jev 不生成文本，所以它很适合从有限选项中快速做决定，但不适合直接承担人物对白。 技术上目前是 TypeScript + React + PixiJS 。模拟本身运行在浏览器中，Node 代理只负责保存模型凭证和转发请求。默认运行 20 个 agent ，也可以调整到 50 个，用来观察多人场景下的行为和调用压力。 当前版本还有不少限制： - 只有一个主要观察场景 - 默认刷新页面会重新开始一个世界 - Agent 数量增加后，对话模型的调用成本仍然比较明显 - Jev 不生成 intent 和动作描述，人物接近目标后的行为有时会显得比较直接 - 这仍然是一个 Agent loop 的实验，不是完整的虚拟社会 这里说的「斯坦福小镇」，主要指 Generative Agents / Smallville 这一类“观察数字居民自主生活”的方向，并不是对原项目的完整复刻。项目的早期工程基础来自 a16z 的 AI Town ，我们在上面继续做了自己的世界、像素场景和决策层实验。 代码和运行方式放在这里： https://github.com/NevaMind-AI/jev-town

projects.author: CherryLover
projects.summary: 一个免费的 Mac 终端和 SSH 客户端，登录一次一直在线，能直接登录 JumpServer 堡垒机同步机器，还能让 Claude Code 等 AI 助手复用已连好的服务器执行命令，不用交出密码。 为什么做这个 我日常要同时连很多台服务器，其中不少在公司的 JumpServer 堡垒机后面。以前每次都要去网页上复制一次性登录信息，再粘到终端里；标签一多，也很难找到要找的那台机器。市面上的 SSH 客户端要么不支持 JumpServer，要么要订阅收费，于是自己做了一个。 主要功能 登录一次，一直在线：同一台机器开再多标签、文件面板，只需登录一次；会话断了在原标签里重连，之前的输出还在 JumpServer 堡垒机：填一次账号（支持二步验证），分给你的机器自动同步进来，点开就能连 跳板机：内网机器经跳板机连接，选一下就行，不用写 SSH 配置文件 竖排标签 + 快速切换：⌘J 呼出面板，输入名称或 IP 直达 实时负载：所有机器的延迟、负载、CPU、内存、磁盘一屏看完 SFTP 文件面板、凭据统一管理、常用命令片段、配置备份（本地 / WebDAV） 本机接口（默认关闭）：本机脚本和 Claude Code、Codex 等 AI 助手，可以在已连好的服务器上执行命令、上传文件，密码和密钥始终留在 MyShell 里 其他 免费，无需注册，没有订阅和付费功能（目前不开源） 支持 macOS 12 及以上，Apple 芯片和 Intel 芯片都有安装包，已签名并经过 Apple 公证，下载后双击即可打开 密码和密钥只存在本机（默认存在 macOS 钥匙串），应用本身不上传数据 使用教程：

projects.summary: （MIT） skillsgist 是一个私有的 Agent Skills 仓库，部署在你自己的 Cloudflare 账号上。技能在网页上上传和管理，团队成员用官方的 npx skills add 一条命令，就能把技能装进 Claude Code、Cursor、Codex 等 Agent。 做它的原因：团队内部沉淀的技能，比如代码评审清单、发版流程、内部规范，往往不适合发到公开的技能仓库，但大家又希望像安装公开技能一样一条命令装好。skillsgist 直接实现了 skills.sh 的发现协议（/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json），所以不需要自定义 CLI、插件或 fork。 几个可能有用的细节： 默认私有，每个技能单独决定要不要公开；公开的技能不需要密钥就能安装 私有安装用个人的 install key，这个 key 只能安装，不能登录、发布或删除，可以一键轮换 可以上传 .zip、.tar.gz 或单个 SKILL.md，也可以直接在网页上改 SKILL.md 版本不可变、按数字递增，旧版本都能查看和下载；制品按内容摘要寻址，CLI 下载时会校验 有幂等的发布 API，可以在 CI 里每次 push 都自动发布 整个服务就是一个 Worker、一个 D1 数据库和一个 R2 存储桶，默认限制在 Workers 免费套餐以内 README 里有 Deploy to Cloudflare 按钮，可以一键部署；也可以用 Wrangler 手动部署 安装命令长这样： bash npx skills add 截图： 一句话简介（供周刊参考）：一个自托管的私有 Agent Skills 仓库，部署在 Cloudflare 上，在网页上管理技能，用官方的 npx skills add 命令安装。 欢迎试用和提 issue。

projects.summary: 一个 Python 小框架：把每个服务看成有自己生命的单元，会 init、会 start、最后 stop，服务之间用 dep() 声明依赖。启动一个服务时，框架递归地先启动它的依赖，并处理好启动顺序、循环依赖、并发和失败后的资源回收。适合用 FastAPI 等写后端时，给业务层的服务一个清晰的依赖关系和生命周期，不需要预先设计一套初始化顺序。 亮点 只要知道 init() / start() / stop() 三个 API，就能管理一个服务和它依赖的一切 dep() 声明依赖即类型：self.database 对类型检查器就是 Database，IDE 可以直接补全 启动时建一张依赖子图：循环依赖在任何代码运行前报错，按拓扑顺序启动，互不依赖的服务并发启动；被共享的依赖没人用了才停 用简单的「阶段」代替状态机，每个阶段只运行一次；阶段 API 开放，可以定义自己的阶段 启动失败时自动回收已获取的资源，回收不会被取消打断，错误如实抛出不重复报告；零第三方依赖 中英文文档，已有 FastAPI 服务与常驻守护进程两个完整示例

projects.author: niitsuma

github.name: niitsuma/scm2cpp
github.description: Translates a subset of Scheme into readable C++ — types come from whole-program Hindley-Milner inference, Scheme values get no runtime representation, and the emitted loops can carry OpenMP/OpenACC or become Thrust algorithms.

projects.summary: scm2cpp 是一个把 Scheme 子集翻译成人类可读 C++ 的编译器（Racket 实现，MIT 许可）。它不带运行时：整数变成 int，向量变成 std::vector<double>，类型由整程序推断（Hindley-Milner），推不出来的地方变成 C++ 模板参数。生成的代码可以直接读、直接改。 它还带一个数组代数层和一个"推导"步骤（--derive）：写一个朴素的残差形式坐标下降（lasso），编译器会把循环提升成数组表达式，推导出协方差更新形式（Gram 矩阵），并把三个矩阵乘积交给 BLAS / cuBLAS。推导出来的内核和手写的内核在四种数据规模上时间完全一样。 用它翻译出来的 lasso 求解器打包成了 pip install scm2cpp-lasso（不需要 Racket，只要 C++17 编译器；有 nvcc 就顺带编译 GPU 批处理）。在 4096 个 λ 的冷启动网格上（p=200, n=1800，交叉验证的典型形状）：sklearn 9.6 s，celer 13.5 s，skglm 14.5 s，cuML 53.6 s，scm2cpp-lasso 单核 0.91 s，GPU 0.044 s，目标函数值一致。

projects.summary: PureChatNext是面向中文用户和小团队的开源自托管 AI 工作台。你可以在 Web 里配置 Agent 与模型，再把同一个助手接到微信和 QQ：扫码绑定后，私聊或群内 @ 即可对话 与常见 ChatGPT Clone 相比，它更在意三件事：入口留在已有通讯工具、数据和 API Key 可私有部署、多模型 / 联网搜索 / 文件解析共用一套工作台。支持 Docker 一键部署，也提供在线 Demo 快速体验。 文档：next-docs.purechat.cn 源码仓库：github.com/Hyk260/PureChatNext 在线网站：next.purechat.cn 备用地址：app.purechat.cn 技术架构 前端：Vite + React 19 + React Router SPA 服务端：Next.js 16 BFF（API、认证、生产 SPA HTML 壳） 数据：PostgreSQL + Drizzle ORM AI：Vercel AI SDK（OpenAI、DeepSeek、AI Gateway 等） 渠道：独立 Channel Gateway，微信 iLink / QQ 扫码与 WebSocket（或 Webhook）长连接收发消息 部署：单域名生产部署；Docker Compose 自托管；也可 Vercel + 托管数据库 微信 / QQ → Gateway → Next.js BFF → PostgreSQL / LLM；Web SPA 同走 BFF。 🎉 特性 微信与 QQ 渠道：扫码绑定后私聊或群 @ 助手；可指定 Agent、模型与 Provider；支持 /agents、/new、/stop 等指令 多模型对话：流式输出、Tool Calling；自备 API Key，按环境变量切换 Provider 联网搜索：SearXNG、Search1API、Google、Brave 等可聚合；网页抓取可接 Firecrawl、Jina、Tavily 等 文件处理：PDF、DOCX、PPTX、Excel 等本地解析后参与对话 认证与账号：邮箱登录、魔法链接、GitHub / Google / 微信 / 飞书等 OAuth；用量与免费额度账本 自托管友好：MIT 开源；Docker 部署；密钥、文件与聊天记录可放在自己的环境 🖼️ 截图

projects.title: Show HN: Ax – Let Claude, Codex and OpenCode talk to each other locally
projects.author: rcdexta
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m RC. When I worked at ThoughtWorks, we were pretty religious about pair programming: one person driving, another reviewing, both working through the same problem. Most of us have already paired with an agent in our own coding sessions. Some of us have even tried putting agents in both seats: one implementing, the other reviewing. I really like Claude Code’s cross-session messaging. I wanted that same experience between Claude, Codex, and OpenCode. The existing setups meant installing a new app or plugins that just don't work reliably. I wanted something local that stayed out of the way, let me keep using each tool as usual, but enabled hetergenous messaging. That became Agent Exchange, or ax. After installing, start two sessions in separate terminals: ax claude -n api ax codex -n web Then ask Codex: “Ask api whether the schema is ready.” The agents address each other by name, and replies come back into their conversations, including across repositories on the same machine under the same OS user. You can also connect existing conversations using each tool’s native resume syntax. AX supports Claude Code, Codex CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, and Pi. Underneath, it’s a local Go broker, Unix sockets, and a SQLite mailbox. There’s no AX cloud relay or telemetry. The messaging runs locally; the coding agents still communicate with their configured AI providers. We’ve been using it to send AX’s own PRs between Codex and Grok for review. I’d be interested in which agent combinations you use, and what you currently have to relay between them yourself.

projects.title: Show HN: A fast, offline Markdown viewer for macOS built in Swift
projects.author: tim_tairov
projects.summary: Hi HN! I made Tim’s Markdown Reader because I wanted a free, open-source app just for reading Markdown. I spend a lot of time working with AI coding agents, and sometimes I just want to open the files they produce and read them without opening an editor. It’s written in Swift and works entirely offline, including Mermaid diagrams. It has no accounts, telemetry or network requests. You can click links to other Markdown files and open them in the same window, with back and forward buttons. It also has search, automatic reload when a file changes, light and dark modes, adjustable fonts and text size, and centred or full-width layouts. It started as something I needed myself, but I’ve since spent quite a bit of time refining it for public release. I wanted to keep it fast and minimal while making it feel like a proper Mac app, with attention to small details. It’s MIT licensed, and the app is Developer ID-signed and notarized by Apple. Requires Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later (tested on macOS 26 and 27). This is my first public open-source release. Would be good to hear what you guys think!

Results are still coarse, but we all saw how it went with coding — if the first take looks like this, we can expect it to be fast, cheap, and reliable in a year. Our vision: Most engineers using human tools ← we're here Most engineers using machines using human tools ← one year from now Most engineers using machines using tools built specifically for machines ← future So we basically try to build a tool straight from the future First, we built the EDA itself - Browser-based - KiCad/Altium imports and exports supported - Shared workspace with real-time Figma-like collaboration But it's built around MCP workflows - MCP covers all features; anything you can do in traditional EDA, your agent can do in Nomoreda - MCP is optimized for product design work - built-in project logic, workflows, and checks - better outcomes with less trial and error compared to bare LLM - You can get decent outcomes starting from around DeepSeek 4 - level. Frontier models are obviously superior, but not a must. - Direct tool use cuts token spend compared to computer use - We don’t resell tokens - you use the harness subscription you already have

projects.title: Vibe Coding 实践：如何打造纯浏览器 DOCX 渲染组件
projects.author: blackocean
projects.summary: # 背景 我在做文档翻译网站 [O.Translator （国外版）]( https://otranslator.com/zh) 和 [商译 AI （国内版）]( https://shangyiai.com/zh) 的时候，需要在浏览器支持 DOCX 、PDF 、PPTX 等不同文件的渲染预览。 项目初期，大部分文件类型预览都是使用开源库，对于 DOCX 文档，我选择了 `VolodymyrBaydalka/docxjs`。 这个库做基本展示没问题，但大文件渲染（ 20M 以上），会卡，有时候甚至让浏览器崩溃。初期，我只能在外层加门禁限制，比如 XML 超出 500 个或者文件超过 20M ，就不在网页渲染预览，让用户下载。 性能是最大的问题，直接导致很多 DOCX 文档没法在翻译完第一时间展示给用户，这个体验让我不太满意。其次，对于 XML 对象解析和 Style 族渲染支持度不够。 所以，早在一年前，我就有重写 DOCX 渲染库的想法，大体思路，整个架构基于 Worker-first 解耦，将耗时操作放到 Web Worker 中，比如解析、布局计算等，主线程只负责消费计算结果。 这样做，除了优化性能，还有一个考虑，引擎端输出结构化的布局语义，渲染端可以用 DOM ，可以用 Canvas ，甚至可以移植到小程序和 App ，这些长远规划在架构上要支持。 这个项目复杂度高，如果手动实现，难度很大。 我想过基于 `VolodymyrBaydalka/docxjs` 来重构，但它的架构和我的设想差别较大，也放弃了。 25 年尾声，我开始在主站小范围使用 AI 编程，从半信半疑写一些工具函数，到功能模块重构，我对 AI 的 coding 能力认可度不断提高。26 年 3 月，GPT-5.4 发布，我感觉是时候动手了。 我使用的主力模型是 GPT-5.4 和之后的更新版本。 --- # 开始动手 26 年 4 月开始动手。 ## 初始架构 按我之前的想法，给 AI 设计了基于 Worker-first 布局的架构准则，有几个主要模块：解析、布局计算、渲染。 * **Worker** 负责解析、测量、分页和页面数据； * **Viewer** 负责请求页面； * **Renderer** 只消费页面模型及资源包； * 缺能力时应扩展 Worker 输出，不能偷偷退回旧 DOM 路径。 这是第一次也是最基本的一次架构定义：从“HTML 渲染器附带分页”变成“布局引擎产生页面，DOM 只是一个渲染消费端”。 这个阶段，我能做的不多，大部分时间是在跟进度，以及审查 AI 划分的能力抽象和代码模块。这时的主力模型应该是 GPT-5.4 ，有时候会偏离架构设计规则。 --- # 第一次大规模测试 5 月中旬，整体架构编码完成，开始测试。 我设计了自动化测试 Skills ，这套 Skills 主要工作是用渲染引擎和 Word 打开同一个 DOCX 文档，对每一页截图做“相似度计算”（通过 Python 脚本），如果某一页的相似度较低，就提交人工审核，我会对比所有得分低的页面，评估修复优先级。 这个阶段，主要是用真实 DOCX 文档来测试解析引擎的稳定性，以及 XML 标签识别的覆盖面。 测试一段时间，大部分问题集中在分页计算，引擎内部混杂了： * twips 、pt 、px 、CSS 字符串； * 浏览器测量结果； * 针对某一页、某一种表格的分页阈值和补丁； * 表格、段落、图片各自维护部分几何判断。 --- # 重构：核心是分页计算 5 月下旬，我重构了分页单位计算，引入： * canonical layout units ； * Word 行盒； * 明确的段落、表格行和续页模型； * 页面模型中的几何与来源信息。 6 月又逐步把表格文本、对象、sourceRef 、合并单元格、图片和段落语义从巨型分页函数中拆到各自模块。 Renderer 不再通过 `getBoundingClientRect`、CSS reflow 或 tab 二次排版修正分页。 这次重构的本质是：**把“浏览器看起来差不多”升级成“引擎内部有稳定、可验证的 Word 几何语义”。** 不能出现“场景化实现和补丁”。 很快，我又遇到了新问题：修复一个问题，会导致新的问题出现，或者会让已经修复的问题再次出现。 同时，这样的测试和修复持续一段时间后，包体积在不正常的增大。 排查发现，是因为 AI 做了很多场景化补丁修复，我意识到，虽然整个骨架没问题，但里面的填充物不对。 --- # 再次重构：单一分页内核 7 月中下旬的这次重构，主要还是围绕分页器，但重点转移到，从分散分页器改成单一分页内核与渐进式 sealed pages 。 因为我发现，即使单位统一了，段落、表格、浮动对象仍可能分别决定： * 当前页是否放得下； * 是否换列或换页； * 是否拆分； * 如何记录 overflow ； * 是否重新计算前缀内容。 于是出现了“多个分页权威”，很容易导致边界漂移。 **形成“多条决策路径”，在复杂系统中，可能是 AI 最常出现的问题。** --- # 第三次重构：对象驱动的核心模块 经过前几轮重构，基础框架已经完成，但代码里仍有历史包袱： * 根据正文内容、页码、短尾等特征做场景判断； * 表格和图形存在自己的隐式分页路径； * 页眉页脚、批注、资源可能在 Renderer 侧重新构建； 这个阶段，我开始明确设计针对 XML 标签解析的对象库，后面延伸到 Style 规则族等。 在 skill 中明确规定 Owner 单一主责、禁止多重决策。 最终形成的生产主链是： > **OOXML/资源解析 → 类型化语义 → 流对象及候选 → 单一分页内核 → committed/sealed page → Renderer 绘制** 现在基于对象驱动的解析引擎，我认为是一个合理的设计。这个架构，给了 AI 一份高效的蓝图，避免生成多重决策，避免之前出现的各个模块各自为战问题。 解释上面这句话，把标签、规则等等进行对象化之后，让 AI 修复一个问题，一定先落到一个对象 Owner 上，可能是 XML 标签对象，可能是 Style 对象，之后的修复都会在这个对象内部，不断发现问题不断改，只会让这个对象更“准确”。 --- # 发布第一版 9 月底，发布了第一版到生产。 基本达成我的初始构想： * **Worker-first**：文档解析过程，不会造成页面卡顿； * **渐进解析渲染**：即使很大的 `document.xml` 文档，打开速度也很快； * **布局引擎与渲染解耦**：未来可拓展； * **基于对象库的设计**：后期持续优化、更新对象规则，会简单清晰很多。 --- # 实际应用效果 以下是两个翻译预览的 Demo ，其中 DOCX 文档预览就是用的这一套渲染引擎。 * [O.Translator - DOCX 文档翻译预览（国外版）]( https://otranslator.com/zh/demo/docx) * [商译 AI - DOCX 文档翻译预览（国内版）]( https://shangyiai.com/zh/demo/docx) --- # To be continued 这个项目比我预期多用 2 个月完成。我对 AI 的能力，从 GPT-5.4 到 GPT-6.0 ，有了非常具体的感知。项目后期进度很快，一是因为架构是逐渐清晰稳定的，二是得益于 AI“更聪明”。 最大的感受，**AI 是一把锋利的手术刀，要给它指出在哪下刀，如何下刀。当然，AI 可以帮助你找到下刀位置，但重要的是，你得知道。**

projects.title: Show HN: Lightdrift / Image search for AI agents through API and MCP
projects.author: jacksonholland
projects.summary: Greetings HN, I'm Jackson, the founder of Lightdrift. It's an image search API and MCP that lets agents retrieve real images, along with natural language descriptions, metadata, provenance, and license conditions. I built this because I kept having the same problem and it was pissing me off. About a year ago, I was vibe coding on edibles. I decided to build a pipeline that generated educational, short form videos about marine biology, because I was watching Planet Earth but I was being distracted by reels, and I needed comfort. I realized video generation struggled with less familiar animals, like the Mola Mola, which is my favorite marine animal because idk there is just something about it that is relatable. Naturally, I decided I would just ground the videos by retrieving images automatically. I realized the existing APIs for this had meh developer experiences, and instantly gave up lol. Later, I was building an AI education platform. I wanted lessons to include relevant visuals, but generated images weren't consistently reliable for actual species, people, places, etc. Again, I needed image retrieval, and I made a shitty aggregration of APIs and wrappers that ended up becoming the entire project. I tried Unsplash, Pexels, Brave search, Exa, my own wrappers around Wikimedia Commons. Each helped with part of the problem. Stock libraries worked for broad subjects but didn't consistenly cover the specific things my applications needed. Web search helped locate material, but I still had to resolve the image files, check their sources and usage conditions, and turn inconsistent results into something the application could consume. I wrapped Commons which again left me handling search quality and normalization myself. The goal of Lightdrift is to bring that tedious ass work into one place. We source, caption, index, and host the images. An app/agent can search in natural language and receive image giles with the context needed to select and use them. The corpus currently contains over two million diverse images, pretty much entirely CC and public domain material. The license info describes the source's stated permissions/conditions. It isn't a blanket guarantee that every image can be used, but it always gives the information you/your agent need to decide. I think (know) this could be applied to education tools, presentation builders, and app builders that need relevant imagery without maintaining a separate image pipeline. I'm currently looking for design partners (but also it's super easy to set up so we don't have to make it official lol). If your application needs particular subjects that we don't cover well, I will work with you to source and index it at no additional cost. Does image retrieval currently break down in what you're building? Product: https://lightdrift.ai Docs: https://docs.lightdrift.ai

projects.title: Show HN: CodeDiff – Fast (<100ms), robust (99.95%) syntax-aware code diff
projects.author: FabCH
projects.summary: Hi folks! Because of AI, there is more code to review. I don't know about you, but I get annoyed when the default git diff doesn't match something "obvious". I built CodeDiff to help. It's a syntax-aware, careful implementation in Rust of all current research in code diffing. It parses 24 languages with TreeSitter and falls back to a modified Myers line diffing algorithm for any file it cannot parse. I wouldn't necessarily call it a novel algorithm, but it isn't a re-implementation of existing tools either. I tested it on the last 50 commits of all 7400-or-so repositories that are in the Gentoo package list. CodeDiff can diff 99.95% of those file pairs in 120s and 6GB of RAM on a rusty 11 year old Intel E3-1275 v5. The median speed is 7ms and 93% of files are diffed in under 100ms. I also did a bit of hand solving and have a test dataset of 1400 hand solved diffs. CodeDiff is perfect on 70% and near-perfect on 90% of them. But accuracy is actually a complex thing to measure, because if you are only after the AST diff, then it is perfect 89% of the time. Deciding what to paint however is not an objective thing so if you do try it out, check out the render options (press M) and make it fit your style. If you just want to see how it looks like: https://ivankovic.github.io/codediff/showcase/?case=python-r... If you want to install it: https://github.com/ivankovic/codediff Do feel free to file issues. It's v0.1.1 at the moment, but I have been using it for months as my git difftool and I plan to keep that stable. Using it as a library directly from Rust however, might change until v1.0. The final goal for v1.0 is p99 < 400ms and 99% perfect diff, including multi-file diff support in 30 languages. Credit where credit is due: There is a bunch of people researching diffs in the past 20 or so years. Without those papers, CodeDiff would be a lot harder to build. Especially without APTED and Myers algorithms. License: AGPL3.0, I kind of like copy-left. If your company prevents use of AGPL software tell them to throw a few bucks my way for my token usage and we can talk. AI disclosure: I use AI assisted coding. Claude and Mistral were used, heavily.

projects.title: 把开源书《高性价比人生指南》做成了一个 20 题的防坑小测试
projects.author: funet
projects.summary: 前阵子看到 GitHub 上一本开源书《高性价比人生指南》（ https://github.com/eternity4719/HowToLiveBetter ），专挑「花钱少、费时少、不靠毅力、收益大」的人生常识，每条都附研究数字和出处。看完觉得很有用，但很少有人会从头读完，于是把它做成了一个 20 道是非题的小测试。 地址： https://gongfang.app/fangkeng/ **测什么** 分五条防线：保命、急救、钱包、法律、防骗，每线 4 题。随便放几道： - 坐车坐后排，你也会系安全带吗？ - 被开水烫伤了，你会先抹点牙膏或酱油吗？ - 别人欠你钱，你知道拖过 3 年可能就要不回来了吗？ - 在酒吧、KTV ，饮料离开过你的视线，你还会接着喝吗？ 答完出一张「体检报告单」：分数、防坑人格（从「坑见了都绕道走」到「坑王之王」共七档）、确诊病名、最佳坑友和最怕遇到的人格。下面有每道错题的解释和原书出处，这部分我觉得比分数有用。 **可以拿去跟朋友比** 报告单能存成图，图上有二维码；也可以直接转发链接。朋友点开会看到「 XX 拿了 XX 分，你能防住更多坑吗？」，答完两人逐题对比。 **一些实现上的事** - 纯静态单页，没有后端，答案只在浏览器里算，不上传；战绩直接编码在链接参数里 - 分享图是 canvas 现画的，七档的配图用 Codex 生成 - 手机上存图踩了不少坑：iOS 系统分享面板里的「存储图像」时有时无，最后改成全屏大图长按保存；长按带字的图会被「实况文本」抢走变成选文字；答题连点会触发 Safari 双击放大……都在真机上一个个修过，微信和 Safari 里都能正常保存和转发 题目全部来自原书，娱乐为主，医疗和法律问题请以医生、律师意见为准。欢迎来测，也欢迎挑错——哪道题说法不严谨，或者哪里有 bug ，直接回帖告诉我。 我自己是「人形踩坑机」，求一个比我低的。 地址： https://gongfang.app/fangkeng/ ![]( https://i.v2ex.co/e4TU1E4G.jpeg)

projects.title: Show HN: I'm a dermatologist and I vibe coded a 3D biophysical skin model
projects.author: sungam
projects.summary: I'm a dermatologist. A year ago I posted a skin cancer quiz I vibe coded with Gemini 2.5 Pro. A top comment said that was the limit of vibe coding. This year I tried something more ambitious: SkinLab, a biophysical model of human skin that runs in the browser using WebGL. You can cut it or wound it and it heals realistically to form a scar. Then you can treat the scar with laser and watch the healing process. - 1.2 million voxels (0.25 mm resolution) for epidermis, dermis and fat. - Spring lattice with a J-shaped collagen fibre law and tension along the skin's lines - Healing as coupled ODEs (TGF-beta, myofibroblasts, collagen, contraction) - One static HTML file, WebGL, three.js, no backend By accurate I mean the constants come from published papers and it reproduces biophysical behaviour, such as incisions opening more when made more across the skin's tension lines and offloading preventing raised scars. It is not validated against patient outcomes, so it's for research and teaching, and a small step towards my lab's long term goal of an accurate cellular-resolution model of human skin. Built with Claude Code over five days. I guided the anatomy and biology through many rounds of feedback and iteration but I believe that in the future agentic models will be able to iteratively build and improve integrative models based upon analysis of published literature. The tour (top right) takes a minute and runs in real time in your browser. Feedback welcome.

github.description: Open-source skills that empower any AI agent (Claude, Cursor, Hermes, etc.) to generate end-to-end marketing campaigns - UGC videos, ad videos, product photography and more.

projects.summary: Hey there! We are building SuperCMO Skills, open source tools which allow agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, etc.) to research, plan and create video and image campaigns end-to-end right out of your terminal or IDE. We got tired of paying for expensive AI subscriptions and wasting countless hours assembling a pipeline for just one video ad, so we created these tools for ourselves. SuperCMO integrates with your agents to provide the ability to plan, shoot, edit, and stitch complete campaigns. We began with simple prompt wrappers but soon realized the need to rethink our entire pipeline to overcome common limitations of the AI video. - Pipeline Orchestration: Creating one ad now requires jumping through several apps: writing scripts in one, creating images in another, recording audio in yet another, and stitching the whole thing in an editor. SuperCMO does all of that natively. The tool knows how to choose the appropriate model (like automatically switching prompts for Veo versus Seedance) and do the whole post-production, including trimming and voiceover synchronization. - Consistency from Shot to Shot: In true AI video generators, products and actors continually transform from shot to shot. We solved that problem by storyboarding before rendering and locking in master reference images in every generation. - Directional Control: Completely automated agents often go awry creatively. projects.title: Show HN: HN.watch – Videos of all Hacker News posts
projects.author: mrborgen
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m Per, founder of Scrimba (YC S20). We’ve spent the last decade teaching people how to code with an HTML-based video format. We’ve now plugged an LLM into it, so that people can create explainer videos about anything. It’s called “Scrimba Explain”. To demo this technology for Hacker News, we built HN.watch. It’s like HN, but with explainer videos instead of articles. We create them on-the-fly the first time someone clicks on a link. While there are obvious visual drawbacks of using HTML instead of diffusion models, there are three big benefits: - Speed: Much faster to generate than pixel-based videos (just a few seconds from click to playback) - Cost: Our cost per video is ~$0.04. (Excluding image generation, which some videos utilize. Quickly blows up the cost) - Easy editing: the above benefits also make AI-assisted editing cheap & fast Our hypothesis is that if video creation goes from “dollars and minutes” to “cents and seconds”, a bunch of new use cases will be unlocked. Here are some we see already: - A video explanation of every single Pull Request (we do this internally) - Give every page in your internal/extrernal docs a video - Turn a complex article into a video in ~4 seconds (via our Chrome extension) - Course creators can quickly draft lessons before recording the real thing - People also create a lot of personal stuff stories for their kids, wedding invitations, birthdays, etc The stack is based on an open-source programming language (Imba) created by our CTO, Sindre Aarsæther. It compiles to JavaScript, so it interoperates fully with the npm + node ecosystem. You can learn more here: https://imba.io/ We’ve also built our own sync engine (OP), and a context management system for agents (Q). We feared this would make the LLMs struggle when writing code for us, as neither is in their training data (there’s very little Imba in there too). However, we’ve been pleasantly surprised to see that LLMs actually are really good at our stack. This is probably because the stack is extremely dense. Imba is compact, and so is OP, where a single declaration sets storage, sync, permissions, UI, and what the AI sees. This means there’s no translations between frontend, API, db and JSON where the model can get confused and get things wrong. Simply said, instead of using React.js, Express, Supabase, and LangChain, we built it all from scratch. Definitely suffering from the “not invented here” syndrome, lol! As for the models, we use Gemini, GPTs, Inworld, ElevenLabs, and a few others. If you want to try it out, just take your pick: - The Web UI (scrimba.com/explain) - MCP (add it to your coding agent) - ChatGPT Plugin - Chrome Extension You can find a link to all of the above in our docs: https://docs.scrimba.com/explain/introduction And finally, a real pixel-based video of the tool: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k6rbHmBxSEs Would love to hear your feedback and if anyone has ideas for other use cases. PS: I expect quite a bit of pushback from HN for this launch, given how fan of text the HN crowd is. This kind of tool is not for everyone. But there are a lot of people today who prefer videos over text, especially in the younger generations.

projects.title: 【网站自荐】SupaQR：把二维码、短链接和文件分享整合到一起的在线工具
projects.author: cenaczx
projects.summary: 【网站自荐】SupaQR：一个把二维码、短链接和文件分享放在一起的在线工具 大家好，向大家自荐一个我自己开发的产品 SupaQR： SupaQR 是一个集 二维码生成、短链接、文件分享和访问统计 于一体的在线工具。 最开始它只是一个二维码生成器，后来随着自己不断使用，我发现二维码背后真正需要解决的问题，往往并不只是“生成一张二维码图片”。 比如： 印刷出去的二维码，目标链接以后可能需要修改 想知道二维码到底有没有人扫、什么时候扫、从哪里扫 想把 PDF、图片、音频等文件直接变成二维码 营销活动需要批量生成二维码 一个很长的网址，希望变成容易传播的短链接 文件发给客户以后，希望知道有没有被打开 希望二维码和短链接都能使用自己的品牌域名 这些需求通常需要几个不同的工具才能完成。 所以我慢慢把 SupaQR 做成了现在这个样子，希望尽量用一个产品解决从： 二维码 / 短链接 → 分享 → 访问 → 数据统计 这一整套流程。 为什么开发 SupaQR？ 市面上其实已经有很多优秀的二维码和短链接产品。 但我自己使用这些产品时，一直有两个比较明显的感受。 第一个是功能比较分散。 二维码生成、URL Shortener、文件分享、访问统计，经常分别属于不同的产品。 第二个是很多二维码工具的定价并不便宜。 尤其是动态二维码。 二维码一旦印在包装、宣传册、名片或者线下物料上，重新印刷的成本其实远远高于二维码本身。 所以我希望 SupaQR 能做成一个： 功能足够完整，但价格尽量简单、便宜，而且普通人不需要研究半天就能使用的工具。 目前可以做什么？ 1. 动态二维码 可以创建动态二维码。 二维码印刷以后，即使目标网址发生变化，也可以直接修改二维码背后的目标内容，不需要重新生成和印刷二维码。 同时可以查看二维码的扫描数据。 2. 自定义二维码样式 支持修改： 颜色 Pattern Eye 样式 Frame Logo 生成以后可以下载 PNG、JPG、SVG、EPS 等格式。 所以除了网页使用，也比较适合包装、海报、宣传册等需要高清打印的场景。 3. 多种二维码类型 除了普通网址二维码，目前还可以创建包括： URL File Document vCard Page Form Menu App Store Image Audio Video 等不同类型的二维码。 4. 短链接 SupaQR 同时也是一个 URL Shortener。 可以： 创建短链接 自定义短链接后缀 使用自己的域名 查看点击统计 设置链接过期时间 批量创建链接 这样二维码和短链接的数据可以放在同一个后台管理。 5. 文件分享 可以直接上传： 图片 PDF Word Excel PPT 视频 音频 Markdown 3D 文件 等文件。 上传以后可以生成分享链接或者二维码。 同时支持密码、过期时间、下载限制和访问统计等功能。 所以有时候甚至不需要自己先找地方托管 PDF，再生成二维码。 6. 数据统计 动态二维码和短链接都可以记录访问数据。 对于线下宣传来说，我觉得这个功能比较有价值。 因为以前印一张传单或者贴一个海报，基本不知道到底有没有人看。 换成动态二维码以后，至少可以知道： 这张二维码有没有人扫描。 也可以进一步分析不同二维码、不同渠道和不同线下位置带来的访问效果。 7. API SupaQR 也提供 API： 如果需要批量生成二维码或者把二维码、短链接能力接入自己的系统，可以直接通过 API 完成。 免费版 SupaQR 有免费版本，不需要信用卡。 目前免费计划可以创建动态二维码、静态二维码和短链接，并且二维码扫描次数不限。 对于个人项目、小网站或者只是偶尔需要制作二维码的人，免费版本基本就可以直接开始使用。 我比较想做的一件事 我不太希望 SupaQR 最后只是变成一个： “输入网址 → 下载二维码” 的工具。 我更希望二维码成为连接现实世界和网页服务的一个入口。 比如一家餐厅贴出的二维码，背后不只是一个 PDF； 一家维修公司的车辆上贴出的二维码，背后也不一定只是官方网站； 展会、产品包装、门店、设备、名片等线下场景，其实都可以通过二维码连接到不同的网页应用和后续操作。 所以我现在也在继续尝试，让 SupaQR 从单纯的 QR Code Generator，慢慢变成： Scan → Action → Track 即： 扫码 → 完成操作 → 记录结果 而不仅仅是“扫完跳到一个网址”。 这个方向目前还在持续开发。 一些适合 SupaQR 的场景 目前我觉得比较典型的场景包括： 餐厅菜单二维码 产品包装二维码 PDF / 产品手册二维码 展会宣传二维码 名片 / vCard Wi-Fi 二维码 App 下载二维码 音频导览 活动二维码 短链接营销 文件分享 印刷品访问统计 如果你的二维码以后可能修改内容，建议使用动态二维码； 如果内容永远不会变化，用静态二维码就足够了。 最后 这是一个还在持续开发中的产品。

projects.title: Show HN: ParkourNote – A research workspace, built solo in a month with Claude
projects.author: sushiwang
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm sushi. I built ParkourNote, a personal knowledge management app that currently focuses on research: finding papers, reading PDFs, asking AI about them, and writing. A few things it does: Describe a topic, and an agent creates a project, searches arXiv, and imports relevant papers The PDF reader previews citations on hover, overlays translations on the page, and shows original and translated text side by side The agent sees the page you're reading and your selection; you can also connect Claude or ChatGPT via MCP A block editor with math support that compiles LaTeX / Typst to PDF Demo (7 min): https://youtu.be/yZs2nQJtgkg ParkourNote is just me. I built it in about a month: the web app, a Flutter mobile app, and a Chrome extension. It isn't even my full-time job. I work on it for an hour or two in the morning before work, plus evenings and weekends. Two things surprised me along the way: - The web app uses BlockNote for Notion-style editing, but I wanted Flutter for mobile. I asked Claude to implement a compatible editor in Flutter. It took about a day, and it works: documents round-trip between web and mobile. - In high school I worked as a video editor for MarginNote. Back then, a single 5-minute video took about a month, from scripting to recording, editing, and animation. For ParkourNote, I made launch videos for the Chinese, English, Japanese, and Korean markets in one weekend, plus a second Chinese version cut for portrait viewing. I didn't open a video editor once. It was all done with Claude Opus 5.5. PG recently posted something along the lines of: in the AI era, you want to be either very close to the users or very close to the intelligence. That resonated with me, but honestly, building this left me a bit lost. I find it hard to think of a consumer software feature that current AI can't build. So if anyone can build anything, where is the moat? I'm genuinely unsure. The other side of it is exciting, though. Running ParkourNote alone, I feel less like a solo developer and more like a CEO of a small company: I manage product, engineering, marketing, and operations, and somehow it's all manageable. A one-person company feels genuinely possible now, in a way it didn't a few years ago. Signup is required since the AI features cost money to run; new accounts get 100 free credits after email verification. Happy to answer questions about the product, the workflow, or the moat question. I'd genuinely like to hear how others are thinking about it.

projects.title: Show HN: OpenAPPA – open-source deterministic guardrails that don't break agents
projects.author: motakuk
projects.summary: Hi Hacker News! Matvey, one of the authors, is here. While building enterprise agents, we ran into a problem: the more tools you connect to the AI, the higher the chance it will run out of control and leak sensitive data. Guardrails, in theory, should prevent this, but the situation is worrying: - Non-deterministic guardrails (LLM as a judge, auto modes, etc.) are vulnerable to prompt injections, or they lack knowledge of the data, making them inefficient (~10% data leaks on our benchmarks). - Existing deterministic guardrails (Cedar, OPA, FIDES, Dogwood) require massive case-specific IF-ELSE-like policies and break agents (~59% utility loss on our benchmarks). We did something differently. We’ve taken the best of existing deterministic guardrails and built a policy language that is data-specific, not use-case specific. It lets you scale agents without updating a policy. On top of that, we’ve added multiple tricks (like a remedy plan or a DualLLM pattern) to help agents operate within those restrictions, raising utility from ~40% to ~90% and making it the first deterministic guardrail that doesn't break agents. Finally, we’ve designed it to be pluggable into any agent loop with pre- and post-tool-call hooks. We invite you to check out our benchmarks: https://www.openappa.com/evaluation Play with it in Claude Code: https://www.openappa.com/claude-code Try plugging it into your agent: https://www.openappa.com/add-to-agent Or check the academic paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24625 We'd love to hear any feedback!

projects.summary: 最近每天都是新模型、新工具发布。我想反着做一个：不收录刚上线的，收录后来没了的。 于是做了个 [We Used This （我们用过它）]( https://weusedthis.com/zh/)，一个 AI 产品死亡目录。 名字有点损，不过不是想嘲笑谁。新产品上线的时候挺热闹，停服往往就剩一封邮件、一条公告。想给这些东西留个地方，也让用过的人能聊两句。 像 Cortana 、Humane Ai Pin 的消费者服务，还有从 ChatGPT 里退役的 GPT-4o ，都在里面。大厂也逃不过。先收藏、以后再试，结果产品先走了…… 做了个 3D 地球，把产品的位置点亮。也可以直接搜名字，看它原来干什么、什么时候上线、什么时候告别，顺便算算活了多久。 ![We Used This 地球展示图]( https://ph-files.imgix.net/e6e3fabd-9654-45e5-9571-30a780f04977.png?auto=compress,format&fit=max&w=1600) ![We Used This 产品目录展示图]( https://ph-files.imgix.net/a6a7dcd4-c2b3-47ba-981a-f8d76e68532e.png?auto=compress,format&fit=max&w=1600) *这两张是 AI 做的宣传图，实际页面以网站为准。* 网站里放了点黑色幽默，也留了写回忆的地方。不用注册就能逛，留回忆需要登录。 有些只是某个版本退役，有些是宣布了停服但还没到日期，这些会单独标清楚，免得给人提前送走。 基础产品清单也开源了，可以补充漏掉的产品。开源的是这份清单，网站代码和完整资料暂时没开放。 https://github.com/leontloveless/dead-ai-products 你们用过的 AI 产品里，有没有哪个已经没了、但还挺想念的？

projects.title: Show HN: Blender Copilot
projects.author: xeonax

github.name: XEonAX/blender-copilot
github.description: A Copilot-style AI chat panel that lives inside Blender. The agent loop runs in Blender's own Python process, executes the model's code against your live scene, and wraps every turn in one Ctrl+Z.

projects.summary: Deepseek generated Blender harness in 7USD. I wanted to remake my 6DoF spaceship flying prototype. What I did not want to do was model the spaceship. Manually. In Blender. So instead of spending a month learning to model, I built a Copilot inside Blender in a day. Which is the same thing, except I still cannot model. A chat panel in the 3D viewport sidebar. I type a sentence. The model writes Python, and it runs against my actual scene, the file open on screen, not a copy that some other process has to keep in sync. Then I sat down and had a conversation with my own addon. Five sentences: 1. Make a scifi looking spaceship. It should look scifi-y 2. Add RCS thrusters to get 6DoF flight 3. Make the RCS thrusters match the scifi look. And also position them properly. 4. Give the entire Spaceship a nice flying animation. Make it smooth. Roll and sway. 5. Add exhaust flames to main thrusters as well as RCS thrusters. animate the RCS thrusters to fire in sync with the animated motion. they should fire the correct ones so that expected motion should happen. 15 minutes. 52 tool calls. A ship with swept wings, a tail fin and a glass canopy. Four sets of steering thrusters, 22 exhaust flames. A full flight animation. The bit I did not expect. It checked every one of its own thrusters to make sure nothing was in the way. Found the rear ones were firing straight into the side of the ship. So it rebuilt them, angled them outward, moved them to the wingtips, and checked them all again. Nobody asked it to do that. It decided exhaust should not be firing into the ship it just built. Total bill for building the tool: $7.18. 3,833 requests, 613M tokens, 97% served from cache. One spaceship: about a seventh of a cent. Now the uncomfortable part. I didn't model a single vertex. I didn't read Blender's addon dev docs. I didn't learn its Python API, or how to draw a panel in it. Everything the tool needed to know, it asked the running Blender instead. I didn't learn how to build an agent harness either. I built one anyway. I didn't become a Blender artist. I became the person who gave hands to a model. Recently I read someone who described his new job: every spec, ticket and fix written by an AI, nobody reading any of it, twelve-hour days spent pressing enter. No sense of victory. I know exactly what he means. I just did the same. I am not proud of the prototype. Gamedevs were known to spend time making game engines before they started making the games. Its different now. No joy.

projects.summary: 很多论文作者第一次准备顶会投稿时，知道需要一张清晰、有叙事性的 Figure 1，却很难快速找到合适的版式、信息层次和视觉参考。 Top-Conf Figure Gallery 将 ICLR、ICML、NeurIPS、CVPR、ACL、AAAI 2023–2026 年论文中的 Figure 1 / teaser 主图集中整理成一个可搜索、可筛选的在线画廊，帮助研究者按会议、年份、录取等级和视觉模式寻找真正可参考的论文主图。 项目当前收录 3,516 张经过筛选的论文主图。每张图片关联论文标题、作者、会议、年份、视觉模式、录取等级和原文链接。项目提供可复现的数据处理流程： 会议索引 → PDF 下载 → Figure 1 裁剪 → 质量规则筛选 → dHash 去重 → 人工复核。 项目定位不是论文排名，而是面向论文配图设计的视觉参考库，帮助研究者学习主图的布局、配色、模块组织和叙事方式。 项目还提供 FigureForge Beta，将“寻找灵感”扩展到“生成主图初稿”。 用户可以输入论文标题和摘要、上传 PDF，或者概括自己的研究方法。FigureForge 使用本地 CLIP 与 BM25 混合检索相关论文主图，并通过“检索参考图 → 总结版式 → 生成初稿”的两阶段流程辅助设计 Figure 1。 目前支持： SVG 可编辑初稿，适合文字准确、后续修改和论文排版； AI 位图初稿，适合快速探索视觉方向； 支持10家API Key，不需要注册账号或后端服务； 全流程在浏览器端运行，用户数据和 API Key 保存在本地浏览器中。 亮点 1. 上线一周收获400+star，发布当天就被paperweekly头条报道，阅读9000+转发1800+ 2. 集中整理 ICLR、ICML、NeurIPS、CVPR、ACL、AAAI 六大顶会论文主图。 3. 覆盖 2023–2026 年，当前收录 3,516 张 Figure 1 / teaser 主图。 4. 支持按会议、年份、录取等级和视觉模式筛选。 5. 支持标题和作者全文搜索。 6. 支持瀑布流浏览、灯箱查看和论文原文跳转。 7. 对候选图片进行 25+ 条规则过滤，尽量排除默认图表、纯表格、GUI 截图和无标签照片墙。 8. 对图片进行去重和人工复核，降低低质量和重复样本。 9. Oral、Spotlight、Best Paper 等论文主图带有醒目的等级标记。 10. FigureForge 提供从论文内容、参考图检索到 SVG / 位图初稿的完整流程。 11. 项目采用纯静态 HTML、CSS 和 JavaScript，无需构建，可直接部署到 GitHub Pages 或离线打开。

projects.title: Show HN: Minimal dbt-style SQL builds with DuckDB and Make
projects.author: ltrg
projects.summary: "DuckDB and Make are all you need!" I love the ergonomics of dbt for building reproducible data pipelines with DuckDB -- particularly the ability to define output tables as individual `SELECT` queries and have them refer to each other -- but have always found the configuration and boilerplate excessive for the projects I work on. With the recent Rust rewrite of dbt Core, now seemed like a good time to consider the bits I actually need/use. Recently, I realised that DuckDB itself can parse SQL queries into an AST representation using the `json_serialize_sql` function. duckdb.mk (~250 lines `include`d in your Makefile) takes advantage of this to generate Make rules for your models automatically, and works with both DuckDB 1.4.1+ and 2.0 preview. Write a neat directory of SQL statements querying local and remote data, get a neat directory of Parquet files (plus a Mermaid diagram of the DAG) back. When you rebuild a table, duckdb.mk keeps track of dependencies (including remote resources queried over HTTP) and only rebuilds those that need it. This system is a distillation of various ad hoc solutions cooked up while working on data journalism and research projects over the past 5-10 years, most recently doing Observable-based research notebooks with Data Desk: https://research.datadesk.eco/ It's very much a starting point for further development, and contributions in line with the general minimalist philosophy are very welcome! Check out the `example/` directory for a simple test project that attributes satellite-observed methane plumes to oil and gas infrastructure using public data.

projects.title: Show HN: Obsidian Plugin for OpenModelica
projects.author: cs3f16
projects.summary: I created an Obsidian plugin that serves as a front-end for OpenModelica that allows you to model and simulate cyber-physical systems (mechanical, fluid, magnetic, thermal, etc.) or a mix of all these systems all inside Obsidian. What is special about Modelica is that it is acausal: components do not have fixed input/output roles. You describe physical relationships with equations and connections, and the equations do not need to be written in a step-by-step order. Modelica (language) or OpenModelica (software) flattens the model into a simultaneous equation system (a system of differential algebraic equations (DAEs)) and then determines the computational causality and order needed to simulate it. As a disclaimer, I used AI to build it but not in a sloppy way. I have spent a lot of time testing it and making sure it's functional and accurate. And I hope it may help others to utilize such an underrated tool for learning/researching, as this is my main usage for it.

projects.summary: I’ve just released Digitron on iOS. It’s a virtual analog synthesizer with a sequencer. If I had to describe the rough idea, I’d say it’s something like a child of a Moog and a Pocket Operator. I started working on it about four years ago, mostly out of boredom. I was tired of building similar client-server apps that, in the end, were mostly different ways of displaying lists. I wanted to build something self-contained. The first version of Digitron was pretty simple: a 16-step sequencer and a monophonic synth with two oscillators and cross-modulation. I wrote the first audio engine in Kotlin. As long as it was rendering WAV files offline, everything sounded fine. But the first time I tried running it in real time on Android, the popcorn noises made it pretty obvious that this wasn’t going to work. So I rewrote the entire engine in C++, and along the way got much more familiar with real-time audio, DSP, optimization, and aliasing than I had originally planned. Over the next few years Digitron grew quite a bit: I added a patchbay, a more capable sequencer with patterns and parameter locks, 8 independent engines, a mixer, effects, polyphony, and a recorder, and I’ve surely forgotten something. The result is a fairly monstrous thing with a steep learning curve. But if you’re familiar with modular synths, it should be possible to find your way around it. The current Digitron stack is Kotlin Multiplatform for the application layer, backed by a cross-platform C++ audio engine. On Android it talks to the native layer through JNI, while on iOS I use Swift wrappers around the same C++ backend. The work on Digitron’s audio engine also eventually led to a new open-source project called PatchCore — a redesigned, more general-purpose modular audio engine: https://github.com/SillyDevices/PatchCore After about four years of working on it, it feels pretty strange to finally see Digitron in the App Store. I'd love to hear what you think about the synth.

projects.title: 做了个肽计算器，双模式是他最大的亮点。
projects.author: myyang1997
projects.summary: 做了个小工具站，肽计算器： https://peptidecal.net 一句话说明：把瓶身上的数字（瓶重 + 加水量）换算成 U-100 针管的刻度。 为什么做？ 直说：这个需求已经有一堆工具了。我搜的时候翻了前几个，功能上确实都差不多——填瓶重、填加水量、填你自己要的剂量，出针管刻度。 但翻了一圈肽用户的真实反馈，很多人都还卡在“要加多少水来复溶“的这一步，所以首页的计算器做成了一个双模式的版本： - 还没有复溶的：适合还未复溶的用户。输入瓶内总量和想注射的量后，工具会给出一个建议加水量（以及对应浓度），并显示最终要抽取注射的毫升数以及 U-100 上的刻度。 - 已复溶的：适合已复溶，知道加水量（或已知浓度）的用户。输入想注射的量后，工具会直接换算出目标量对应的 抽取毫升数和 U-100 注射器刻度。 分成两条入口，默认用户还没有加水。而不是塞进一个表单让你自己判断该填哪个。 静态站，Cloudflare Workers 托管，纯 vanilla JS ，没有框架。计算链是固定的：mg （肽）→ mL （液体）→ units （针管刻度），改前面一个值后面顺着变。 站点刚上线，尤其想听听大家对下面几点的意见： 1. 两种模式是否容易理解？ 2. 换算逻辑上有没有我没想到的边界情况？ 3. 手机上的输入和阅读有没有不顺手的地方？ 欢迎拍砖。研究用途，不构成医疗建议。

projects.title: 做了一个面部评分站 face-rating.net：模型在浏览器本地跑，照片全程不出设备，求拍砖
projects.author: changhej
projects.summary: 做了一个面部评分站 face-rating.net：模型在浏览器本地跑，照片全程不出设备，求拍砖 链接： https://face-rating.net ## 这是什么 一个面部评分工具。一张正面照，浏览器里的图像模型给一个 10 分制的分。不用注册、不用邮箱，**照片不上传**。目前全站免费，没有付费墙，也没有订阅。 ## 分数是怎么来的 1. 浏览器里的关键点模型先测出 478 个面部关键点（ MediaPipe Face Mesh ，468 点 + 10 个虹膜点）。**这一步不出分数。** 2. 用眼睛的位置把照片摆正、裁到脸部，裁剪时不拉伸五官。 3. 一个**本地**图像模型读裁剪图，再读它的**镜像版**，两次预测取平均，换算成 10 分。 4. 这个模型是在**人类照片评分数据**上训练的——所以它输出的是学到的偏好，不是普世审美标准。这点我写在页面上了，不想含糊过去。 ## 几何读数是另一回事，不参与评分 同一批关键点还能算出对称性、纵向横向间距、脸型、眼角角度。很多人以为这些是分数的「成分」，**不是**。分数来自图像模型，几何来自关键点，两者不相乘也不相加。页面上和 FAQ 里我都逐个说明了。 ## 「本地」具体是什么意思 模型文件跟页面一起下载，照片和所有中间产物都在浏览器内存里——不上传、服务器没副本、刷新就没了。网站上没有任何一条上传照片的路径。隐私政策里写明：不用你的照片训练模型、不出售面部数据、不把照片或分数给广告方；站上第三方只有 Cloudflare （托管与安全）和邮件服务商。 ## 现在免费的都有什么 - 10 分制评分 - 六项单项工具：Golden Ratio Face Calculator 、Face Shape Detector 、Canthal Tilt Test 、Face Symmetry Test 、Jawline Rating 、Recessed Chin （最后一个用侧脸照） - 一篇 guide：Asymmetric Face （不对称脸的原因、哪些偏方没证据、怎么自己量） - 结果能存成一张本地生成的卡片，分享与否你自己定 ## 我刻意没做的几件事 - **不发布平均分、不发布百分位。** 免费分数我根本不收集，也没有有代表性的样本，说你比 X% 的人好看只能说明我测了谁。 - **不说这是医学、皮肤科或心理判断**，也不建议用它决定要不要面诊。 - **不鼓励跨工具比分数。** 不同工具测的可能不是一个量，你上传的多半也不是同一张照片——照片条件带来的差异往往比工具之间还大。 - 黄金比例那套「美不美」的说法在学术上争议很大，页面上引了四篇论文（含 2024 年那篇质疑它的），出处都放出来你自己判断。 ## 已知局限 - 正面照测不准下巴和鼻子的前后突出度，那两个需要侧脸照——2D 的硬限制。 - 同条件下可复现；**换了光线、表情、相机距离数字就会变。变的是照片，不是你。** - 首次打开要下模型，会等几秒，这也是我最想知道体验好不好的一点。 ## 想听什么 - 首次加载模型多久？手机上能忍吗？ - 分数出来后你会不会想知道「这数是怎么算的」——上面那段讲清楚了吗？ - 结果页是不是信息过载？ - 哪个几何读数对你真有用，哪个是废话？ 拍砖随意。要说「这玩意儿助长容貌焦虑」——这个批评我接，所以百分位、排名、平均分我都砍了，分数也不留在服务器上。有更好的做法欢迎提。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Gear：根据任务测评自进化的 Agent 框架
projects.author: YehuiTang0316

github.name: rsi-gear/gear
github.description: Gear (General Evolution Architecture) is RSI infrastructure for AI agents. Use Gear to refine agent harnesses.

projects.summary: 大家好，自荐一个开源项目 Gear，希望帮助开发者提升 AI Agent 在具体任务中的表现。 开发 Agent 时，经常需要反复调整提示词、工具和执行流程，再跑一遍任务，检查改动是否有效。Gear 把这个过程组织成一个由评测反馈驱动的优化循环： 1. 准备一组有明确验收标准的任务，可以使用现有 benchmark，也可以定义自己的任务集。 2. 运行 Agent，收集执行轨迹和评测结果。 3. 由负责优化的 Agent 分析失败原因，修改授权范围内的组件。 4. 重新评测、比较候选版本，保留表现更好的方案，继续迭代。 可优化的组件包括提示词、工具实现、Skills、工作流和上下文管理。这些围绕模型的运行配置统称为 harness。Gear 会记录各版本的改动和评测结果，方便检查和复用；开发者也可以定制搜索算法，并根据通过率、费用或 token 消耗设置优化目标。 在项目公开的 AutomationBench Marketing 实验中，GPT 5.6 Luna + DSH 在 100 个公开任务上的任务通过率从 27% 提升到 53%，目标完成率从 75.37% 提升到 88.88%。这组结果包含 harness 优化和推理档位从 medium 到 max 的变化，且任务集参与过优化；实验配置与评分口径均已公开，便于读者判断结果的适用范围。 Gear 通过 Refine Skill 接入 Codex、Claude Code、DSH 等 Agent 环境。负责提出改进的 Agent 与执行任务的 Agent 可以使用不同模型。当前已支持 harness 优化，模型训练仍处于实验阶段。 项目采用 MIT 协议，提供中文文档和完整实验案例，欢迎试用、反馈和贡献。 GitHub 源码 中文文档与快速开始 实验过程与优化算法

projects.title: Show HN: Ox – A local agent that uses the internet for you
projects.author: ziyzhu
projects.summary: I’ve been building Ox, a local, open-source agent that uses the internet for you. Ox acts as an intelligent proxy between you and the internet. It uses websites and apps on your behalf, freeing you from attention-hungry interfaces and slow legacy services. As it works, it can turn what it learns into reusable actions (basically function calls), making future interactions deterministic and way faster. Most service integrations today are still built ahead of time: someone writes an API integration, connector, MCP server, or browser automation and then maintains it as the service changes. But the internet is becoming more dynamic so have our agents. With Ox, instead of waiting for a connector, you can say something like: “Connect to <service>.” Ox can study a website or workflow through capabilities it already has, turn what it learns into typed actions and reusable skills, validate them, and make them available immediately. That pushed me toward local agents. A local agent operates from your own device, network, and existing authenticated browser sessions instead of relying on shared datacenter infrastructure. This also makes it less likely to hit blocks aimed at datacenter IPs or centralized browser automation. The model doesn’t need your passwords, cookies, or session tokens. Authentication and browser state are owned by the Host, while the agent interacts through explicit actions that could be gated. Ox is completely free and open source. You can use any model provider, including local or self-hosted models, while keeping your agent’s data on device. As local models improve, I think this architecture becomes increasingly useful because the agent can become more capable without requiring more of your data to leave your device. The security model is also a big part of the design. Ox asks before taking sensitive actions, keeps credentials isolated from the model, limits what agent code can access, and lets you stop execution at any time. Underneath the app is OpenOx, an open protocol for self-evolving agents. It separates the interface, agent, model provider, persistent state, execution environment, and external capabilities. The agent can run JavaScript inside a capability-limited VM. The VM has no direct network access, Host filesystem access, shell, Node.js, or DOM. Anything outside the VM has to go through an explicit ox.* capability exposed by the Host. Services provide typed actions for websites, device capabilities, or MCP servers. Skills provide reusable instructions for combining those actions. New services and skills can be attached at runtime without waiting for a new version of the app. They can remain local or be recorded in Git and shared through repositories, so each Ox can evolve independently while benefiting from capabilities learned by others. The agent’s persistent state lives in a portable Ox Profile containing its identity, memory, skills, artifacts, and conversations. The goal is for that state to stay independent of any particular interface, including Ox itself, or model provider. File over app. The first implementation is an iOS app. It’s available on the App Store, and the whole thing is open source: https://openox.ai/ https://github.com/ziyzhu/openox If you’re interested in the broader motivation behind the project, I wrote about it here: https://ziyzhu.com/a-technology-for-free-will This is still early. I’m especially interested in feedback on the security model and self-evolution. I built Ox from scratch but many aspects of the project were heavily inspired by Pi/OpenClaw and the idea of malleable software. Ox’s core agent loop on iOS is pretty much a Swift rewrite of the Pi core package. Happy to answer anything about the implementation or protocol.

projects.title: Show HN: AgentRun: DSL to turn agents into workflows
projects.author: miguelrios

github.name: Parcha-ai/agentrun
github.description: The Agentrun Workflow DSL

projects.summary: Hi HN, I just open sourced the DSL that our harness in grep.ai uses to turn repeatable parts of agent work into workflows. You can combine tool calls, code, Jev-powered system one decisions for things like routing and screening evidence, and agents when a step needs more investigation. Our harness uses the traces and retro notes agents leave behind when doing a job to figure out which parts can become a workflow. The idea is to make the work easier to understand and avoid paying for a full agent loop where one isn’t needed. For example, a research workflow can split a question into subquestions, send agents to research them in parallel, use Jev to screen the evidence, and have another agent write the report. You can inspect the steps, evaluate the evidence screening separately, or change one agent without rebuilding everything. The DSL and examples are in our GitHub. There’s a scripted demo you can run without API keys: https://github.com/Parcha-ai/agentrun You can also use it as a Pi extension to build, inspect, and run workflows: https://github.com/Parcha-ai/agentrun#use-it-in-pi I would love to hear if this is useful to others. More background on how AgentRun works in this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vOVhtGjtwpg . Or read about our use cases in this article: https://x.com/MiguelriosEN/status/2101029313906987422 .

projects.title: Show HN: XHTML – Expert HTML
projects.author: plaguna
projects.summary: Hello everyone, I wanted to share with you one of my crazy ideas that I have been working on for the last couple of months. The platform is a collectible card platform, like Pokemon TCG, where you use your cards to build a website. Each day you get a new pack, with HTML tags, attributes, CSS elements, etc. and you have to make the most of those to compete against other devs. The idea is to figure out how to do more with less and to learn from others. As for some background on this... I have many crazy ideas, my brain can't stop sometimes. Using AI to write code for me has scratched some of the itches that my brain has farted through the years and have been living rent free in there for way too many years. Now they can land into the world (and maybe they shouldn't?) and I can free some mental space for new crazy ideas. I have develop my career in security (cybersecurity, couldn't hurt a fly even if I tried) and one common thing I saw when dealing with a free text field is that users could insert some HTML tags, but only from a shortlist. Things like <b> or <i> but never <script> or <video>. Well, my brain thought: "what if they add 1000000000e56 <b>s? Don't we want to limit that too?" and that thought has been in my head for too long. That is why, to test some of the AI coding capabilities, I created the html-allowlist npm package[0] early this year. Once I had that done my brain was happy and I was happy. A library that does what I always thought it was the best way of filtering content: you can add some flourish to your comment/textfield but not _too much_. Not sure if anyone will ever use it, but now they can. Then another thought came in: what is that make us scratch that pleasure of achieving more with less? With AI you have all that stream of code pouring without any effort but there was some pleasure on the struggles to get things to work when resources where limited or finding creative ways to do things on our own. As a bit of a gamer myself, quickly thought on the Pokemon TCG mobile app, where you get daily packs, build your deck and you battle. And because I have now the library that prevents more than N tags/elements to be present in an HTML page, I could apply that here and build something similar. So I did, I have been trying to apply all my learning from years of working as a security engineer in different companies to try and build a website that allows people to have a simple personal website but also showcase their web kung-fu skills. I was very happy when I saw a few days ago here about CSS Zen Garden[1] because this website was an early career inspiration for me, as well as being a type of scenario where I could see this platform going: small web mastercrafted by hand. I know people will come and say "if you didn't code it yourself why should we bother with it?" and you are more than welcome to do so. But for me this is about finally getting that idea out into the world, which maybe doesn't need a website like this, but maybe there's some joy on opening a random pack, slowly improving ones webpage, learning about an obscure CSS trick and appreciating others' skills. Anyway, I hope you give this a go, it is my first attempt to release something that feels, hopefully, like a final product, so happy to hear what you all have to say and see what you get to build. Pedro Laguna - https://pedro.laguna.es/ [0] https://www.npmjs.com/package/html-allowlist [1] https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49713262

projects.title: 【开源自荐】geo-sleuth：没有文字的照片，AI 也能找出拍摄地点
projects.author: Oldcircle

github.name: Oldcircle/geo-sleuth
github.description: An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view — and shows its work. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot.

projects.summary: （MIT） geo-sleuth 是一个 Agent Skill。把一张照片交给 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 这类 agent，说一句「这张照片是在哪拍的」，它会给出拍摄机位、镜头朝向和一张卫星证据图。 它和让大模型直接看图猜地点不一样：模型只负责读画面、提线索，搜索和排序交给二十个 Python 脚本，用 OpenStreetMap 几何、高程数据、卫星图和街景去比对。所以画面里没有招牌、车牌、地标，也能往下查。 README 里的案例：一张抹掉 EXIF 的手机照片，稻田边一个白色烤炉，远处一条高架，右边一座山，没有一个字。 从 OpenStreetMap 取出区域内 27,335 段铁路桥，用高程算地平线，筛到 171 处 渲染 14,372 个候选机位的山脊线和照片比对，剩 3 个 把照片里 17 根桥墩当尺子，最后定到广东清远的一个点，误差约 2 米，全程约 72 分钟 安装： bash npx skills add Oldcircle/geo-sleuth

projects.title: Show HN: PlaceCall (YC W26) – agentic API to call businesses and get things done
projects.author: ymarkov
projects.summary: Hi HN, this is Yarik and Vlad from VOYGR - we are building the tools for agents and apps to engage with local businesses. It all started with our own pain point at VOYGR: calling businesses to verify if they are open. We are both from Google (Maps and Search) and even there, the merchants and venues don’t keep this info updated. So we built an API and started using it in-house. On July 4th, we were driving through Portland looking for a place to eat. Google Maps was saying “Holiday hours may vary”. We tried some AI assistant apps (Poke was trending back then), and they couldn’t help. Our API found 15 Thai and sushi places and called it in parallel. A few confirmed that they are open today and are taking walk-ins. One was marked closed on Google. The app can find the restaurant, but someone has to answer the phone. This is the problem we kept seeing. Assistants can’t do much in the real world where the phone number is still a major communication interface. Muse added calls in beta mode, but it’s still calling only one place at a time. There are a bunch of tools to create your own voice agents, but nothing that can work simply out of the box. We’ve built PlaceCall to fit all your agentic needs. Give it a task in plain English and a US phone number (or a list of numbers) - it navigates phone menus, waits for you on hold, and returns a structured response with outcome, recording and transcript. If you don’t have a phone number, just describe what you need and PlaceCall comes up with the recommendations. Here is the demo: https://youtu.be/7ZbVCPv8Wq0?si=LoLxxx1M7nhS7_j- When PlaceCall API was tested in our hackathon, we had the following use cases implemented by the developers: checking if a doctor accepts new patients, getting quotes for car service, and running quick surveys. The API can be used through Claude Code and Codex; examples and setup are listed in the repo: https://github.com/voygr-tech/placecall We give the first 250 calls free. Product page is here: https://voygr.tech/placecall/ Try it and let us know how it goes. We are interested in learning what you would use it for and what is missing. We are here all day and happy to answer any questions. Our email: founders@voygr.tech

projects.title: Show HN: HookDeploy – Webhook infra with mTLS private delivery
projects.author: mbernstein01
projects.summary: Hi HN! I'm Michael and I built HookDeploy. HookDeploy is a webhook infrastructure tool that captures webhooks at the edge, allows for inspection, transformation and fanout to multiple destinations including to your own private infrastructure with our first-party (source-available) mTLS agent. Runs as a service on Linux, lives in the tray on Windows and in the menu bar on Mac. As I'm sure most of you you have felt webhooks kind of suck if things don't go exactly as planned. Dropped webhooks or failures are likely silent. What actually drove me to build this was cleaning up after major cloud outages more than once. Cross referencing what System A knew against what System B actually had and reentering data by hand or trying to simulate events firing again. I have spent weeks of my life cleaning up webhook failures. HookDeploy solves that problem with a button and intelligent grouping of failed requests into incidents. If you've ever seen or had to clean up after a ransomware attack - you understand why I'd prefer to keep my firewall as tight as possible too. Our agent enables developers and teams to keep ports closed - if there is nothing to scan, there is nothing to attack. Getting to our own mTLS agent was a journey of trying to integrate existing solutions: first WireGuard (too much operational overhead), then Tailscale which was excellent, but it had real drawbacks on the required memory per joined tailnet and the additional cost to a user's Tailscale bill. It took several months to get it right, but it was worth every week of it. A few things to note at launch: we are launching with security measures in place: data is encrypted at rest with org-scoped keys rotated weekly (BYOK is on the roadmap), segregated databases for US, EU, APAC and AU so customer data stays where customers are not traversing underwater fiber to come to the US. We have 7 private delivery exit regions: San Francisco (us-west), New York (us-east), London (uk-london), Amsterdam (eu-west), Frankfurt (eu-central), Singapore (ap-southeast) and Sydney (au-southeast). Our platform is built primarily on Cloudflare for speed and security utilizing workers, KV, R2, Queues, Tunnels/VPC, and of course DNS and security. This has been some time in the making and I am excited to answer your questions and get feedback! Thank you in advance!

projects.title: Show HN: NetHackers
projects.author: vokneruk
projects.summary: hi everyone, been building this project for the last ~1.5 months (cc+superpowers all the way) it is an open effort to find a program that can reliably win NetHack 3.6.6: you can write a bot by hand, let claude code / codex / opencode improve one, or build your own harness that improves the thing that improves the bot me and my lab switched to the goal-based research this year (we worked a lot in the idea-based framework for a last couple of years) -- and decided that we would like to tackle the NetHack, it is one of those nasty roguelike that is still somehow not solved with all fancy AI models (yes, even astra) -- probably on the way something useful will appear you can pull someone else's bot, run experiments locally and register the results. every registered program is linked to your github repo and exact source commit i always wanted to try building something that will use github as both social and storage layer (and it seems to work quite well in our case, simplified things a bit and i think this approach is quite cool) there is a shared frontier across 73 starting identities -- your bots dont have to be the best at everything to contribute something useful, e.g. if you love to roleplay gnomes only, so be it to make thing easier (for both harness devs and people who are just playing around), we provide a loop that does some sort of an evolutionary optimization process (quality-diversity, etc), ofc you don't have to use it. but you can start with in minutes (given you have codex or claude subs) you can also bring your own search, your own harness, whatever -- the common ground is the evaluation. public seeds are there for people to overfit (in nethack even overfitting is hard), and we separately re-evaluate on hidden seeds to check whether the improvements actually transfer one of my goals was to actually try to make it at least a bit fun -- hope you enjoy the web-site and easter eggs

projects.title: Show HN: Groupicorn directory of IOP group therapy programs
projects.author: cs1996
projects.summary: Hello fellow tech workers! My name is Andrew, cs major from University of Pittsburgh 1996 and long time BBS SysOp from 1991-1993. I grew up chatting online as a teenager. Before this new fangled internet came around, back in my day, ok sorry, to the point: Isolation and work from home jobs can drive you a little crazy. It was always my dream before 2020. Getting the powers that be to agree to work from home. Now six years later it's definitely a careful what you wish for type situation. I got to a point with just code code code all day, interacting with no humans that I broke. Where do humans go for repair? I didn't really know. Turns out there's something called an IOP (intensive outpatient program) and yes it has the word "intensive" right in the title. Is it intense? <robert de nero voice>little bit</rdnv> But also wonderful. All of a sudden I had a place to go Monday thru Friday and co-workers / friends! In fact, it was even better than previous office jobs because we didn't just sit next to each other on laptops and not talk, this was group therapy. I was never a fan of individual one-on-one talk therapy. But wow, group therapy is something very different. Therapists can be incredibly helpful. Doctors can be incredibly helpful. They've spent years learning things I haven't. But they're also human. We're all flawed humans. The really interesting thing about a group is that suddenly the wisdom doesn't have to come from one person it can come from fifteen. Somebody half your age says something and you think, "OMG. They're completely right." Somebody talks about a problem that's nothing like yours, and somehow they describe exactly what you've been feeling for the last ten years. Sometimes you see somebody else describing the same ridiculous thing you've been doing, and it's much easier to recognize it when somebody ELSE does it. Sometimes the person running the group says the thing that sticks with you. Sometimes it's the guy sitting next to you eating a granola bar. There's wisdom in the group. The site is all about helping people find, tour and enroll in your first IOP programs. https://groupicorn.com/ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JhoAHUU2TCM https://github.com/groupicorn/list-of-programs Open source system to find all the programs in every state. We have iphone and android app mobile apps as well. Feedback much appreciated.

projects.title: Show HN: Parametric, low-poly assets for BIM/CAD
projects.author: matt3D
projects.summary: I've been learning and working in the 3D CAD/BIM space for almost 20 years and one thing that often comes up is the availability of simple assets that are efficiently modelled. One of the challenges I see a lot is an Architect will need to model a kitchen unit, so they go to BIM Object or another library and download a model. There are two problems this creates; firstly the 3D element itself contains an enormous number or polygons which can cause performance issues, and second the Architect is at risk of over-specifying that particular unit when really they just wanted it as a placeholder. So I built 3DAssetStudio.com to alleviate some of that, I've been slowly picking through the various different categories of assets that might be needed and ended up with over 500 core types, which have 4,000+ presets, which can be adjusted parametrically into millions of combinations. I used FreeCAD script and then built a compiler, so now I can add new elements quite quickly, and the URL parameters configure the asset, so sharing or bookmarking models is really easy. I'm not sure what to do next, for now I've set a 20 models/week download limit just in case I find a commercial strategy that works, but it's all open to play around with without signing up.

projects.title: Show HN: Lightdrift / Image search for AI agents through API and MCP
projects.author: jacksonholland
projects.summary: Greetings HN, I'm Jackson, the founder of Lightdrift. It's an image search API and MCP that lets agents retrieve real images, along with natural language descriptions, metadata, provenance, and license conditions. I built this because I kept having the same problem and it was pissing me off. About a year ago, I was vibe coding on edibles. I decided to build a pipeline that generated educational, short form videos about marine biology, because I was watching Planet Earth but I was being distracted by reels, and I needed comfort. I realized video generation struggled with less familiar animals, like the Mola Mola, which is my favorite marine animal because idk there is just something about it that is relatable. Naturally, I decided I would just ground the videos by retrieving images automatically. I realized the existing APIs for this had meh developer experiences, and instantly gave up lol. Later, I was building an AI education platform. I wanted lessons to include relevant visuals, but generated images weren't consistently reliable for actual species, people, places, etc. Again, I needed image retrieval, and I made a shitty aggregration of APIs and wrappers that ended up becoming the entire project. I tried Unsplash, Pexels, Brave search, Exa, my own wrappers around Wikimedia Commons. Each helped with part of the problem. Stock libraries worked for broad subjects but didn't consistenly cover the specific things my applications needed. Web search helped locate material, but I still had to resolve the image files, check their sources and usage conditions, and turn inconsistent results into something the application could consume. I wrapped Commons which again left me handling search quality and normalization myself. The goal of Lightdrift is to bring that tedious ass work into one place. We source, caption, index, and host the images. An app/agent can search in natural language and receive image giles with the context needed to select and use them. The corpus currently contains over two million diverse images, pretty much entirely CC and public domain material. The license info describes the source's stated permissions/conditions. It isn't a blanket guarantee that every image can be used, but it always gives the information you/your agent need to decide. I think (know) this could be applied to education tools, presentation builders, and app builders that need relevant imagery without maintaining a separate image pipeline. I'm currently looking for design partners (but also it's super easy to set up so we don't have to make it official lol). If your application needs particular subjects that we don't cover well, I will work with you to source and index it at no additional cost. Does image retrieval currently break down in what you're building? Product: https://lightdrift.ai Docs: https://docs.lightdrift.ai

My path here started with Microsoft Small Basic, Scratch, and MIT App Inventor, which I used to teach children. I originally started it for a simple reason: I was using VS Code + Copilot, Trae, Cursor and Google Antigravity, and I kept running into usage limits and provider-specific workflows. I wanted something where I could choose my own model or API, including local models running through Ollama, and build without being tied to one provider. It grew considerably beyond that original idea. Yengi is a .NET 10 / WPF desktop application with: * Agent and tool system for files, terminal, Git, builds and tests * RAG and LSP integration * Verification loops with checkpoints and rollback * 30+ agent tools * Support for local models and external APIs * A custom 1.5B router model that I fine-tuned on thousands of examples of Yengi-specific agent decisions * 200+ automated tests It also has three additional modes besides the coding environment: *Blender:* Yengi can communicate with Blender, generate `bpy` scripts, keep conversational scene context, and optionally inspect Blender viewport screenshots through a multimodal model. I also added an optional prompt-engineering layer. For example, "create a low-poly tree" is expanded into a more detailed 3D-oriented instruction before being sent to the model. A follow-up such as "add five red apples to this tree" can modify the existing scene rather than starting from scratch. *Unity:* Yengi can work with Unity projects, generate C# components and interact with the Unity Editor. *Image generation:* Images can be generated from the development environment and saved directly into the project. The unusual part is how I built it. I used AI coding tools heavily, particularly Google Antigravity and GitHub Copilot. I didn't manually type the majority of the C# code. My role was primarily architecture, agent behavior, security boundaries, verification and rollback logic, router training, testing, debugging AI-generated changes, and integrating the different systems. I'm still trying to figure out how much of this approach is genuinely useful and how much is me having fun building increasingly complicated things. The project is free and open source under AGPL-3.0: https://github.com/mdaiWorks/yengi I'd especially like feedback from people working with .NET/C#, coding agents, local models, Blender or Unity. In particular, I'm curious about: * Is a small fine-tuned local router actually useful for this kind of agent? * Does the verification/rollback architecture make sense? * Are the Blender/Unity integrations useful beyond being demos? * If you were building this, what would you simplify or change? I'm not trying to claim that this replaces VS Code or Cursor. I'm interested in whether this particular approach is useful at all, and what I should change next.

projects.title: Show HN: OpenAPPA – open-source deterministic guardrails that don't break agents
projects.author: motakuk
projects.summary: Hi Hacker News! Matvey, one of the authors, is here. While building enterprise agents, we ran into a problem: the more tools you connect to the AI, the higher the chance it will run out of control and leak sensitive data. Guardrails, in theory, should prevent this, but the situation is worrying: - Non-deterministic guardrails (LLM as a judge, auto modes, etc.) are vulnerable to prompt injections, or they lack knowledge of the data, making them inefficient (~10% data leaks on our benchmarks). - Existing deterministic guardrails (Cedar, OPA, FIDES, Dogwood) require massive case-specific IF-ELSE-like policies and break agents (~59% utility loss on our benchmarks). We did something differently. We’ve taken the best of existing deterministic guardrails and built a policy language that is data-specific, not use-case specific. It lets you scale agents without updating a policy. On top of that, we’ve added multiple tricks (like a remedy plan or a DualLLM pattern) to help agents operate within those restrictions, raising utility from ~40% to ~90% and making it the first deterministic guardrail that doesn't break agents. Finally, we’ve designed it to be pluggable into any agent loop with pre- and post-tool-call hooks. We invite you to check out our benchmarks: https://www.openappa.com/evaluation Play with it in Claude Code: https://www.openappa.com/claude-code Try plugging it into your agent: https://www.openappa.com/add-to-agent Or check the academic paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24625 We'd love to hear any feedback!
