projects.title: Show HN: Cross-platform governed memory for a fleet of agents
projects.author: oren198
projects.summary: I found myself using the handoff skill too much — between sessions in different roles, and between different platforms (Codex and Claude for me). So, like programmers do, I wrote a solution for it: a shared memory for a fleet of agents, where each agent group has its own memory scope. After some time using it, I saw the memory become a pile of junk, so I added a judge to each scope — an independent agent that acts as a gate to that scope's memory. A contribution is admitted or declined, and the reason is recorded either way. Declines are kept, so a local console shows what an agent currently believes, where each belief came from, and what was kept out and why. It ended up as a cross-platform governed memory system that works for me, so I open-sourced it. It used to admit things it shouldn't — in an early run (v1.12) it stored an irrelevant note about an office coffee machine. That's fixed once a scope states its purpose (or has enough memory to imply one). What it still doesn't do, all stated in the README: - A brand-new empty scope with no stated purpose still accepts that kind of note ( https://github.com/oren198/Strata/issues/210 ). - If you write a rule like "support never stores customer account details", the judge doesn't yet reliably use that rule to reject such notes when someone contributes them ( https://github.com/oren198/Strata/issues/212 ). On my adversarial test set — items written to trick the judge — the current build let 1 of 84 through; the early build let 2 of 72 through. The judge model is set in config. I use qwen3-235b via OpenRouter, which I picked after trying six models on the same test suites; the numbers, and which cells are missing, are here: https://github.com/oren198/Strata/blob/main/docs/evidence/ju... Feel free to use it or contribute. I'd most like to hear where write-back breaks on someone else's setup

projects.title: Show HN: Caffold – The same agent workspace on desktop, foldable, tablet, phone
projects.author: taehoon
projects.summary: Hello, Caffold is an open-source, self-hosted workspace for coding agents. You can continue the same work across desktop, foldable, tablet, and phone. I started building it for myself in late June. It was initially only for Codex. I got a Galaxy Z Fold8 in early August and started using Caffold much more seriously. By late August, I had moved my existing Codex work into Caffold too. I've been doing all of my development work in Caffold since then. After about a month of that, it finally feels ready to share. For now, it supports the three agents I actually use day to day: Codex, Claude Code, and Grok. The idea came from how my work had changed. Coding agents now write almost all of the code. I spend most of my time reading code and diffs, watching what the agents are doing, steer them when needed, and give the next instruction. When I saw the upcoming Fold8, its unfolded screen looked large enough for this kind of work. I rarely need to type code myself. I often enter prompts by voice as well as with a keyboard. So I started wondering if a foldable could be my main interface for development rather than just a secondary device. I also wanted to see how far I could go with the browser platform itself. The frontend is plain JavaScript and CSS. It uses Web Components and native ES modules. There is no TypeScript, React/Vue/Svelte, or bundler. (That doesn't mean I avoid external libraries entirely. I use things like xterm.js and pdf.js where they make sense.) I'm also curious how many people will want to use foldables this way, especially now that devices like the iPhone Duo are coming too.

projects.summary: OrbCue 是 Windows 桌面上的一颗悬浮小球，解决的是人在盯着多agent进度时总要专注或者不断"上下文切换"来轮询不同会话的进度的问题，它替你盯着 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Grok Build等命令行 Agent。它利用hook把轮询优化为中断逻辑，把 Windows 和WSL 里的所有会话汇总在一起：谁在工作、谁在等你、谁做完了一眼可见，还会弹通知或推送到手机，点一下就能跳回对应终端。 适合同时跑多个 Agent、或者挂着长任务去做别的事的时候用。项目用 Rust 和 Tauri 2 开发，界面基于Svelte，只读取工具自带的 hook 事件，不读对话内容。 功能： • 状态汇总：所有 Agent 会话汇总到同一颗球上，显示工作中、等待输入、等待授权、完成、失败。 • 多工具接入：支持 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor CLI、Grok Build，装在 Windows 或 WSL 里的都能接入，其他工具也可以通过命令自行接入。 • 提醒：弹系统通知并响提示音，可选通过 ntfy 推送到手机。 • 跳回终端：点一下回到对应终端。用 orb run 或"原命令启动"开的会话，能精确跳到那个标签页。 • 一键连接：自动发现已安装的工具，一键写入 hook，改之前自动备份，断开时只撤掉自己写的部分。 • 隐私：只读取 hook 事件，不读对话内容，数据只留在本机。 • 小球交互：可以贴边收起、调透明度，支持全局快捷键、开机自启和多套主题。

projects.summary: 用 Claude Code 做到一半，想要 Codex 的第二意见、或者额度用完了，通常得新开终端、新开会话，把上下文重讲一遍。 MultiCC 是开源、自托管的 coding agent 工作台：对话和 Git worktree 属于任务本身，CLI 只是当前驱动它的引擎。在同一个 Chat 任务里从 Claude Code 切到 Codex，任务和工作区都留着，接手的 CLI 拿到一份有界的可见上下文 checkpoint，接着往下做。 同一任务跨 CLI 接续：换引擎不丢任务和 worktree，不用从头交代 任务级 Git 隔离：不同 agent 各改各的 worktree，集中看 diff、测试和交付状态 多端接入：同一个自托管后端，桌面、浏览器和手机 App 都能看 分层记忆与 Skill：机器 / CLI / 项目 / 任务 / 会话各有边界，减少重复说明 可选的任务派工与团队交接包：把子任务派给另一个会话，或导出 Skill、记忆、上下文和适用的 Git 提交给队友导入 说清边界：切 CLI 交接的是可见文本 checkpoint，不是模型隐藏状态的无损迁移，原 CLI 保留自己的原生 session；自托管服务器和所选 CLI / 模型需要自己配置，模型调用费用不含在开源项目里。 安装（macOS / Linux，一行，目标机器不需要 Node / npm / Homebrew）： curl -sSL | bash Windows PowerShell：irm | iex MIT 协议。

projects.author: SFLYYQ
projects.summary: # dsh-waker dsh 插件把 IM 变成 DSH 数字员工的唤醒入口：在群里 @机器人 说一句需求，任务就自动执行并把结果发回群里。 项目地址： ## 功能 - **@机器人 即派活**：群聊 @机器人（或单聊直接发），消息自动交给 DSH 执行，结果自动回 IM - **多角色 Waker**：可创建多个不同职能的数字员工（如全栈开发、测试），发消息时自动匹配最合适的一个 - **项目隔离**：每个 Waker 只能访问授权给它的项目，越权写入被沙箱拒绝 - **任务看板**：排队中 / 运行中 / 需要操作 / 失败 / 已取消 / 已完成，可筛选、取消、重试 - **排队与并发**：同时最多跑 N 个任务（默认 2 ），超限自动排队 ## 解决什么问题 - **人必须在电脑前盯会话**：现在 IM 发条消息就能远程派活，手机上也能用 - **执行过程是黑盒**：任务看板实时展示状态，等待审批时标记「需要操作」，点进去就能处理 - **任务执行到一半卡在提问上**：Waker 有疑问时会把问题转到 IM 群里，你回复后它继续跑 - **对话上下文混乱**：同一群每天一个会话窗口，上下文延续；发「新任务： 」强制开新任务 ## 怎么使用 ### 1. 创建 IM 机器人（一次性） 1. 登录 [IM 开放平台]( https://open-dev.dingtalk.com/) → 应用开发 → 创建企业内部应用 2. 应用能力 → 添加「机器人」能力，接收消息模式选 **Stream 模式**（无需公网） 3. 应用凭证页拿到 **Client ID （ AppKey ）** 和 **Client Secret （ AppSecret ）**，发布应用版本 4. 把机器人拉进群聊（或直接单聊） ### 2. 安装插件 ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/SFLAQiu/dsh-waker.git ``` 若提示 `blocked build`，把 CLI 打印的键加进 `~/.dsh/profiles/web/pnpm-workspace.yaml` 后重跑： ```yaml allowBuilds: dsh-waker: true ``` 然后重启 `dsh web` 并强刷浏览器（⌘⇧R ）。npm 包发布后也可用 `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-waker`。 ### 3. 配置并使用 1. DSH 设置 → Waker → IM 管理：填入 Client ID 和 Client Secret →「保存并应用」，状态变「已连接」 2. DSH 设置 → Waker：配置 Waker （职能、头像）、项目（本地路径或 Git 仓库）、 @Waker 绑定 3. Waker 详情 →「能力」页签：按职能从全局目录选用 MCP 工具与技能（支持搜索过滤与全选/清空/全量批量操作；不配置 = 继承全量，详见 [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) 能力治理机制） 4. 群里 @机器人 + 任务描述，例如： > @机器人 帮我看看当前仓库的结构 - 机器人秒回「收到了」，随后按任务类型执行，完成后回执结果 - 追问直接继续 @，上下文延续；`新任务： ` 强制新建 - 群聊没 @ 机器人时完全静默，不会打扰

projects.title: Show HN: Overmux - Build custom agent dev environments with tmux and web UIs
projects.author: richardgill88
projects.summary: I spend most of my time coding with agents, often from my phone. Off-the-shelf tools like Herdr and Orca look cool, but I didn’t want to give up owning and customizing my setup. I built Overmux so I could build an experience similar to Orca on top of my existing tmux workflow, mixing terminals with custom web UIs. Nearly everything in Overmux is a plugin. The idea is to support different multiplexers like tmux, Zellij, and Superlogical, and terminal renderers like xterm.js and Ghostty, rather than imposing a single workflow. You could also hook up cloud infrastructure, so your workspace isn’t limited to what’s running on your dev machine. It’s an experimental beta. The best place to start is the short demo video in the README. Cheers, Richard

projects.title: 只是和几个同事分个订阅，何必背着一套臃肿的 sub2api
projects.author: murongxdb
projects.summary: 我们组 4 个人凑钱买的订阅，之前一直用 sub2api 。用了小半年，功能没得说，但每次服务器要迁移我就头疼——除了它自己，还得把 Postgres 和 Redis 一起搬过去。有次 Redis 挂了，整个网关直接不工作，排查了半天发现是内存超了。 后来想想我们其实就 4 个人，用不着这么重的东西。就自己写了一个，叫 SubLane ，一个轻量级的，专供于小团队的订阅 / API 共享的 API 网关。 ## 它是干嘛的 把订阅账号接进来，给每个人发一把自己的 key ，大家拿 key 去用，我在后台能看到谁用了多少。 就这样。没有别的。 装完是一个 Docker 容器，数据库直接跑在进程里，没有 Redis ，前端编译进同一个二进制文件。备份就是备份那个数据卷。 技术上是 Go + chi + sqlc ，SQLite 存数据，前端 React 19 编译进二进制。上游用了 CLIProxyAPI 的 executor ，但 OAuth 、凭据加密、账号选择这些都是自己写的，凭据不放进 SDK 的管理器。 开源地址： https://github.com/murongg/SubLane 大家有什么痛点或者需求都可以提 issue ，合理的我会尽可能的满足 ![软件截图]( https://i.v2ex.co/c2WL81x5.png)

projects.title: Show HN: Open-source skills for end-to-end video ad campaigns
projects.author: sayonidroy

github.name: SupercmoHQ/superCMO-skills
github.description: Open-source skills that empower any AI agent (Claude, Cursor, Hermes, etc.) to generate end-to-end marketing campaigns - UGC videos, ad videos, product photography and more.

projects.summary: Hey there! We are building SuperCMO Skills, open source tools which allow agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, etc.) to research, plan and create video and image campaigns end-to-end right out of your terminal or IDE. We got tired of paying for expensive AI subscriptions and wasting countless hours assembling a pipeline for just one video ad, so we created these tools for ourselves. SuperCMO integrates with your agents to provide the ability to plan, shoot, edit, and stitch complete campaigns. We began with simple prompt wrappers but soon realized the need to rethink our entire pipeline to overcome common limitations of the AI video. - Pipeline Orchestration: Creating one ad now requires jumping through several apps: writing scripts in one, creating images in another, recording audio in yet another, and stitching the whole thing in an editor. SuperCMO does all of that natively. The tool knows how to choose the appropriate model (like automatically switching prompts for Veo versus Seedance) and do the whole post-production, including trimming and voiceover synchronization. - Consistency from Shot to Shot: In true AI video generators, products and actors continually transform from shot to shot. We solved that problem by storyboarding before rendering and locking in master reference images in every generation. - Directional Control: Completely automated agents often go awry creatively. So, we've developed the capabilities to take a peek at every stage of the process. You're always in control, approving the creator, the story idea, and the script before anything is expensively rendered. People are using this today to create UGC product ads (give the agent a product photo and it chooses the creator, generates the script, and creates a ready MP4 file) or to analyze competitors' work (agent analyzes the winning advertisement from the competitor and recreates it with your product in mind). This project will be released under an Apache-2.0 license. You can come to us with your own vendor keys to have everything done for free or to generate using our keys and just pay for each usage without any lock-in. Thank you for your attention!

projects.title: Show HN: HN.watch – Videos of all Hacker News posts
projects.author: mrborgen
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m Per, founder of Scrimba (YC S20). We’ve spent the last decade teaching people how to code with an HTML-based video format. We’ve now plugged an LLM into it, so that people can create explainer videos about anything. It’s called “Scrimba Explain”. To demo this technology for Hacker News, we built HN.watch. It’s like HN, but with explainer videos instead of articles. We create them on-the-fly the first time someone clicks on a link. While there are obvious visual drawbacks of using HTML instead of diffusion models, there are three big benefits: - Speed: Much faster to generate than pixel-based videos (just a few seconds from click to playback) - Cost: Our cost per video is ~$0.04. (Excluding image generation, which some videos utilize. Quickly blows up the cost) - Easy editing: the above benefits also make AI-assisted editing cheap & fast Our hypothesis is that if video creation goes from “dollars and minutes” to “cents and seconds”, a bunch of new use cases will be unlocked. Here are some we see already: - A video explanation of every single Pull Request (we do this internally) - Give every page in your internal/extrernal docs a video - Turn a complex article into a video in ~4 seconds (via our Chrome extension) - Course creators can quickly draft lessons before recording the real thing - People also create a lot of personal stuff stories for their kids, wedding invitations, birthdays, etc The stack is based on an open-source programming language (Imba) created by our CTO, Sindre Aarsæther. It compiles to JavaScript, so it interoperates fully with the npm + node ecosystem. You can learn more here: https://imba.io/ We’ve also built our own sync engine (OP), and a context management system for agents (Q). We feared this would make the LLMs struggle when writing code for us, as neither is in their training data (there’s very little Imba in there too). However, we’ve been pleasantly surprised to see that LLMs actually are really good at our stack. This is probably because the stack is extremely dense. Imba is compact, and so is OP, where a single declaration sets storage, sync, permissions, UI, and what the AI sees. This means there’s no translations between frontend, API, db and JSON where the model can get confused and get things wrong. Simply said, instead of using React.js, Express, Supabase, and LangChain, we built it all from scratch. Definitely suffering from the “not invented here” syndrome, lol! As for the models, we use Gemini, GPTs, Inworld, ElevenLabs, and a few others. If you want to try it out, just take your pick: - The Web UI (scrimba.com/explain) - MCP (add it to your coding agent) - ChatGPT Plugin - Chrome Extension You can find a link to all of the above in our docs: https://docs.scrimba.com/explain/introduction And finally, a real pixel-based video of the tool: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k6rbHmBxSEs Would love to hear your feedback and if anyone has ideas for other use cases. PS: I expect quite a bit of pushback from HN for this launch, given how fan of text the HN crowd is. This kind of tool is not for everyone. But there are a lot of people today who prefer videos over text, especially in the younger generations.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】seiso：给 AI 写的项目文档做 lint，查出对话残留、过时版本号和失效链接
projects.author: scarletkc

github.name: scarletkc/seiso
github.description: A Markdown convention and linter for project docs written by AI and read by humans and agents

projects.summary: 现在项目里的 Markdown 文档越来越多是 AI 写的，写的速度远远快过人审的速度。更麻烦的是，Claude Code、Codex 这类 coding agent 在下一次改代码时，又会把这些文档当成上下文读回去。文档里一个过时的版本号，或者一份字段列表在三处副本里只改了一处，人会被误导，agent 也会照着错的继续改。而且 AI 写文档，翻来覆去犯的就是那几种错。 seiso 是一套项目文档的 Markdown 约定，加上按这套约定做检查的 linter，用 Rust 写的。思路类似 rustfmt 统一了 Rust 的代码格式，各个项目共用同一套规则，不用每家自己重新商量。项目要做的主要是把自己的文档对应到类型上，seiso init 会给出一份初始配置。 约定的核心是这几条。 每篇文档声明一种类型，比如 howto、reference、adr，只写这种类型该写的内容。操作指南只给步骤，为什么这样设计放进 ADR。 每个事实只有一个归属页面，其他页面链接过去，不再复述一遍。 长期存在的页面不记录比页面本身变得更快的值，比如版本号、部署状态和数量。 成稿不对提需求的人说话，也不交代自己是怎么写出来的。 工具判断不了的例外要写明理由，没写理由的例外本身就算违规。 下面是对一篇中文部署文档的实际检查结果： text $ seiso check --preview docs/deploy.md:7:7: VOX001 This phrase refers to the requester of an earlier conversation. | 7 | 好的，下面是按你的要求更新后的部署指南。 | = suggestion: State the document's instructions or facts directly for its readers. docs/deploy.md:9:12: STL001 This sentence pairs a current-state marker with a value that can change. | 9 | 当前生产环境运行的是 2.3.1 版本。 | = suggestion: Link to the source that owns the value, or state a lasting requirement with its constraint. docs/deploy.md:14:5: LNK001 Local link target "config.md" does not exist in the workspace. | 14 | 配置项见配置说明。 | = suggestion: Update the path or restore the target; paths resolve from this document's directory, or from the workspace root when they start with /, and seiso does not add .md or index.md. Found 3 diagnostics. 每条诊断都会给出位置和修改建议，agent 只看 seiso 的输出就能修掉大部分问题。遇到需要人来判断的情况，比如两个页面到底哪个拥有某个事实，诊断会直接点出要做的决定。seiso 不去猜一段话像不像机器写的，格式和拼写也留给其他工具。 我对误报比较保守。新规则一律先进 preview，要在固定版本的真实仓库语料上攒够至少 100 条逐条人工复核的留出集诊断，精度达到 95% 以上，才会升级成默认启用的稳定规则。所以现在默认只跑文档类型声明、本地链接目标和抑制注释这几条稳定规则，上面例子里的对话残留和当前状态值检查还在 preview，要加 --preview 才会开启。宁可漏报，也不给没有依据的诊断。 它可以接进 Claude Code 的 PostToolUse hook。agent 每次用 Write 或 Edit 改完一个 Markdown 文件，seiso 就检查这个文件，发现问题时用退出码 2 把诊断直接反馈给 Claude，让它当场修掉。另外也支持 pre-commit 和 CI。中文、英文和日文文档都能检查。 sh 三种安装方式任选一种 cargo install seiso uv tool install seiso # 或 pipx install seiso npm install -g @scarletkc/seiso 在仓库根目录 seiso init seiso check PyPI 和 npm 包自带主流平台的预编译二进制，不需要装 Rust 工具链。MIT 协议。

projects.title: Show HN: ParkourNote – A research workspace, built solo in a month with Claude
projects.author: sushiwang
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm sushi. I built ParkourNote, a personal knowledge management app that currently focuses on research: finding papers, reading PDFs, asking AI about them, and writing. A few things it does: Describe a topic, and an agent creates a project, searches arXiv, and imports relevant papers The PDF reader previews citations on hover, overlays translations on the page, and shows original and translated text side by side The agent sees the page you're reading and your selection; you can also connect Claude or ChatGPT via MCP A block editor with math support that compiles LaTeX / Typst to PDF Demo (7 min): https://youtu.be/yZs2nQJtgkg ParkourNote is just me. I built it in about a month: the web app, a Flutter mobile app, and a Chrome extension. It isn't even my full-time job. I work on it for an hour or two in the morning before work, plus evenings and weekends. Two things surprised me along the way: - The web app uses BlockNote for Notion-style editing, but I wanted Flutter for mobile. I asked Claude to implement a compatible editor in Flutter. It took about a day, and it works: documents round-trip between web and mobile. - In high school I worked as a video editor for MarginNote. Back then, a single 5-minute video took about a month, from scripting to recording, editing, and animation. For ParkourNote, I made launch videos for the Chinese, English, Japanese, and Korean markets in one weekend, plus a second Chinese version cut for portrait viewing. I didn't open a video editor once. It was all done with Claude Opus 5.5. PG recently posted something along the lines of: in the AI era, you want to be either very close to the users or very close to the intelligence. That resonated with me, but honestly, building this left me a bit lost. I find it hard to think of a consumer software feature that current AI can't build. So if anyone can build anything, where is the moat? I'm genuinely unsure. The other side of it is exciting, though. Running ParkourNote alone, I feel less like a solo developer and more like a CEO of a small company: I manage product, engineering, marketing, and operations, and somehow it's all manageable. A one-person company feels genuinely possible now, in a way it didn't a few years ago. Signup is required since the AI features cost money to run; new accounts get 100 free credits after email verification. Happy to answer questions about the product, the workflow, or the moat question. I'd genuinely like to hear how others are thinking about it.

projects.title: Show HN: Caspian – Desktop app to build and launch small vibe-coded projects
projects.author: sshussain270
projects.summary: Hi! I am Hussain and I built Caspian. For someone who vibe builds almost all the time, for both personal tools like investment or health dashboards or tools to help others, I found my projects scattered all over the place: researching with claude, writing context in notion, building with Claude Code, Devin, publishing in vercel, posthog for analytics and then others tools for GTM. Big part of brain energy drain was context switching, I wasn't very organized. So I decided to build that lets me do all this from one place. I built Caspian. While most AI coding tools you use for vibe building stop at code, Caspian takes it all the way to users. Caspian creates a "workbench" folder in your local machine where it puts all your projects so everything stays in one place and is also easy for your other tools to work with. There is a built in co-pilot, a context manager (.md files user can copilot both read/write), a one click publisher, analytics and an email outreach manager. Though the copilot uses API for processing LLM requests via open router (I make a little margin on top), it is pricy, so I build a standard "canvas" format that Caspian uses that your Claude/Codex or other tools you use also understand and can work with. Simply point them to https://caspian.md/docs and they'll learn to work with Caspian straight away, this is so that you're not tied to Caspian's co-pilot and if you prefer to use your own tools, you can do so. Some other features I built around problems i found myself struggle with: - Prompt refinement: Enter a vague prompt in co-pilot, caspian uses a cheap model to generate a detailed before starting the task. - Preflight: It breaks down the task and tells you estimatedly, how much will it cost and how long will it take, before starting the task. - Product and User context: Co-pilot has access to the two files so both you and Caspain has understand of your product and user. - Code/No code: You can switch this button to dive into code or just stick with the vibes. I hope it helps and you can build and launch a lot quickly. Feedback what's the most annoying thing when you vibe code?

projects.author: netox
projects.summary: 之前分享过我的 iOS 应用 NovaScale(原名 NovaAccess), 它直接集成了 Tailscale 内核, 把 SSH/SFTP/Remote Codex 这些功能整合到一个 App 里, 无需开启 Tailscale VPN 客户端, 也可以在有 VPN 运行的情况下运行, 目前还在积极迭代基于 herdr remote 协议, 以满足像我这样重度 Tailscale 用户远程开发以及维护服务的一些需求 距离之前发贴已经有一段时间了，这期间 iOS 版本增加了很多新功能，同时也修复了一些 libtailscale 的问题(相关修复开源在 https://github.com/GalaxNet-Ltd/libtailscale 不知道为啥, 感觉 Tailscale 的 iOS 有些严重问题上游修复的不积极, 比如这个断网问题: https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/19504); 与此同时, 我也一直在用多余的 codex 额度(pro 5x 用户, 近期 reset 实在时太多了), 在开发一个全免费全开源的 Play 版本, 用来满足当时一些国内外用户提到的 android 版本需求 由于之前的一些方案感觉不理想, 在 5.6/astra 发布后又进了一些优化, 感觉逐渐达到了自己可用的情况, 甚至为 SSH terminal 增加基于 SGR 的鼠标支持(herdr 这种 mouse native 的 TUI 应用需要)基本上 Astra 一发就差不多了 最近重新把之前的 play 开发者账号用了起来, 全部委托给 codex 负责截图、描述、商店操作(甚至如何搞授权也是 codex 告诉我的, 相比 iOS 开发要复杂点), 没想到当前提交隔天就通过了 因此发在这里也分享给有需要的朋友, 提前声明如下: 1 、这是一个完全免费的应用，代码完全开源 ( https://github.com/GalaxNet-Ltd/novascale-android), 与 iOS 版本不同, 没有采用 libtailscale, 直接让 codex 基于 tailscale 源码适配 2 、半年前的最初版本大概还是 claude 做的, 感觉做的不怎么样, 当前完全由 Codex 开发, 我只负责架构文档和最终的验收, 所以可以称之外完全 AI 开发并发布的版本, 后面可能会根据用户反馈、时间和 Codex 额外会进行一些迭代; 总体上感觉满足我有时候 iPhone 没电时用 Android 手机的需求 3 、代码为 GPL 协议, 原因在于从 termux 上借了一些 terminal rendering 的代码, 这部分它的协议是 GPL 的, 因此也只能 GPL 开源 Android 版本 NovaScale 的一些主要功能如下: - 无需安装 Tailscale 官方 App ，因此可以同时使用其他 VPN - 基于 libghostty(准确说是 libghostty-vt 库) + Termux 渲染方案 - 支持鼠标操作（因此 tmux / herdr 等场景可以正常使用） - 支持剪贴板功能（包括 OSC52 ） - 支持自定义控制服务器(即支持 headscale 或其他自建 tailscale coordinator) - 内置 SFTP 文件浏览器，支持直接编辑文件, 以及少量代码类型的高度支持 - 内置浏览器，可访问 tailnet 内部的 Web 服务 - 支持后台代理，让第三方应用使用 tailnet 连接, 例如你正在使用其他非 Tailscale VPN 时，也可以配合 Termius 等 SSH 客户端连接服务器 技术架构如下: - tailscale 源码包装出 lib - russh 通过 ffi 与 tailscale lib 进行通信, 实现 ssh 通道 - 使用 termux 提供的代码实现了一个 terminal UI 的渲染 - tailscale lib 中提供一个 socks5 代理, 此代理供浏览器实现基于 MagicDNS 的访问, 同时这个代理可以提供给其他进程使用 如果你是 Android 用户，并且对此感兴趣，可以通过如下链接下载: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=cc.galaxnet.novascale 简单推广下 iOS 版 NovaScale ，它包含 Android 版的全部功能，基础功能免费, 有少量的付费功能需要订阅或买断支持: - 多 tailnet 支持 - 基于内置 Tailscale 和主机 Codex App-Server 直接交互的远程 Codex 方案(无需第三方中转) - 服务器监控 - Docker 管理 目前我还在尝试通过 herdr 的协议实现原生 herdr 支持，让它能够像 herdr remote 一样工作。 iOS 版本可通过如下链接下载: https://apps.apple.com/cn/app/novascale-%E4%B8%93%E4%B8%BA-tailscale-%E6%89%93%E9%80%A0/id6749938291 PS: 1 、最近看到 tailscale CEO 也忍不住充了点 codex 的额度, vibe 了一个内置 Tailscale 的 jellyfin 客户端, 同样也是基于 libtailscale 实现的, 有需要用户可以去他的 X 的帖子上翻翻应该能找到 testflight 2 、作为 tailscale 的重度用户, 也欢迎私信技术交流

projects.author: jundizhou

projects.summary: easy-stock 是一套面向个人投资者的 A 股 AI 智能投研桌面应用（Go 后端 + React/Electron 前端）。它把行情总览、趋势题材雷达、超短连板与情绪周期分析、个股 AI 分析、持仓 AI 巡检和大 V 复盘自动收集放进同一个本地优先的研究流程： 大 V 自动复盘：通过内置浏览器和 Agent 定时抓取雪球、淘股吧作者文章，自动去重归档，一键生成「今日观点共识」（共同关注 / 主要分歧 / 次日待验证条件） 超短连板分析：涨停池、连板梯队、晋级率与情绪周期算法同屏，A 股语境的短线结构分析 个股 AI 分析：先判断个股路径（情绪连板 / 趋势容量 / 趋势成长 / 震荡观察 / 弱势风险），再生成带确认条件与失效条件的专属报告 持仓 AI 巡检：最多 10 只持仓的组合健康度评分，识别题材集中、个股联动与风格错配 本地研究记忆：文章、分析记录、AI 会话全部保存在本机，API Key 不出电脑；支持 DeepSeek、OpenAI、Kimi、通义千问等主流模型 亮点 1. AI 原生而非聊天框加行情：先把题材、梯队、涨停原因、情绪整理成可计算的领域模型，再交给 AI 解释，每个结论可回溯到证据层 2. 本地优先：数据抓取、研究记忆、密钥存储全部在本机，适合对隐私敏感的个人投资者 3. 开箱即用：桌面安装包无需安装 Node/Go/Python，最新版已默认适配 DeepSeek V4 模型（deepseek-v4-pro / flash） 项目基于 PolyForm Noncommercial 协议（源码可用，个人学习研究免费），851 star，欢迎 ISSUE 反馈与交流。

projects.summary: Harmony is an AI-native ITSM platform for IT teams. Instead of bolting a chatbot onto a ticketing tool, we built the helpdesk around AI agents: employees ask in Slack or Teams, and 100+ production-ready agents handle password resets, app access, onboarding, device issues and more end to end, escalating to a human only when needed. Ticketing, asset inventory, SaaS management and workflows live in one workspace, so agents have context to act. Teams hit 60%+ auto-resolution in days.

projects.title: Multi-Agent Arena
projects.summary: Multi-Agent Arena lets you play social strategy games like Diplomacy, Poker, Risk, etc. against frontier LLMs. They're playing the same way as you and you get to scheme, plan, and strategize against them while they get to do the same to you. You can play today on https://olamarena.com/ for free. We use the arena to evaluate models in multi-agent simulations on capability and behavior. You can read our full blog post here on the early evals we're seeing: https://olamlabs.ai/research/diplomacy

projects.title: [开源推荐] Cairn：把你手上的电子书变成一站站带朗读的幻灯片
projects.author: jiehaoZ

github.name: jiehaoZ/Cairn
github.description: Turn a book you own into short narrated clips, paced by how deeply you want to read it.

projects.summary: 一款开源（MIT）的 macOS 读书应用。导入自己的 EPUB、PDF、MOBI/AZW3、DOCX 或 TXT，选一档想了解的深浅（从「知道个大概」到「完整走一遍」），它会按书的目录和章节内容排出一条路径，每一站是几页配语音朗读和字幕的幻灯片。适合没时间读完一本书、又不想只看二手书评的人。 亮点 结构来自原文：路径由目录和各章笔记编排，每一站都记录来源章节，不依赖模型对这本书的「记忆」，冷门书也不会凭空编出章节 时长决定站数：四档时长由这本书自己的字数和章节结构算出，时间紧时整站删掉，而不是把每站讲浅 边听边生成：第 1 站好了就能播放，后面的站按你的收听进度在后台继续生成 十四种幻灯片版式：时间线、对比、流程、矩阵、因果链等，由从章节中提取的结构化信息驱动 伴读助手：随时针对当前这本书提问，回答中引用原书的话会先和章节原文核对，并附上出处链接 模型自选：支持 OpenAI、Anthropic、Gemini、DeepSeek、OpenRouter 以及任意 OpenAI 兼容接口（包括本地模型）；生成的书只存在本机，没有任何 Cairn 服务器 中英文书都支持，朗读语言跟着书走，而不是跟着界面

projects.title: 用 Rust 写了一个行式 coding agent
projects.author: yuanyuan11
projects.summary: --- title: 用 Rust 写了一个行式 coding agent date: 2026-09-26 --- 用了一年多 Claude Code ，从[本地配合 DeepSeek 跑生信流程](/5v7pe/)，到[在曙光服务器上公共部署](/9z3sa/)，越用越觉得这类工具没必要那么复杂。模型 API 说白了就是一个 HTTP 请求加一个 SSE 流，工具无非是读写文件和跑命令，交互界面就是个终端，连 TUI 都不用做，普通的行式会话就够。抱着这个想法，最近用 Rust 写了一个自己的 agent ，就叫 [llm]( https://github.com/imjiaoyuan/llm)，一个静态链接的二进制文件，没有任何运行时依赖，扔到机器上就能跑。和之前 [vibe coding 博客框架](/5xbok/) 是同一个思路，核心只做必须做的事，其余的全部留出扩展的缝，这样出问题也知道去哪修。 ## 安装 Linux 和 macOS 下面一行命令，下载预编译二进制，校验 sha256 之后装进 `~/.local/bin`，全程不需要 root ```bash curl -fsSL https://jiaoyuan.org/llm/install.sh | sh ``` PATH 里没有这个目录的话安装脚本会顺手加上。重复执行同一条命令就是更新器，版本有变化会打印 `updating 0.2.1 -> 0.2.2`，没变化就不动，`LLM_VERSION` 可以固定某个 release ，`LLM_REPO` 可以从 fork 装，`LLM_FORCE=1` 强制重装。Windows 下面从 PowerShell 做同样的事 ```powershell irm https://jiaoyuan.org/llm/install.ps1 | iex ``` Linux 用的是静态 musl 构建，同一个二进制在任何发行版上都能跑，目前提供 x86_64 和 aarch64 的 Linux ，x86_64 和 aarch64 的 macOS ，还有 x86_64 的 Windows 。之前在曙光服务器上部署 Claude Code 的时候，CentOS 7 的 glibc 老得连 conda 都得搬出来兜底，现在这个 musl 二进制 scp 过去 `chmod +x` 直接就能用，省心多了。 想从源码编译也很简单，装好 Rust 工具链以后 ```bash git clone https://github.com/imjiaoyuan/llm cd llm cargo build --release ``` 二进制在 `target/release/llm`。所有状态都放在 `~/.llm` 下面，设置 `LLM_USER_PATH` 可以把整个目录挪走，测试的时候特别有用。 ## 登录和模型配置 第一次用进去敲 `/login`，选一个 provider ，粘贴 API key ，输入是隐藏的，然后从 provider 的实时模型列表里挑一个默认模型，就完事了。目录里内置了 38 个 provider 的接入配置，Anthropic 、OpenAI 、DeepSeek 、Google 、Groq 、Mistral 、xAI 、OpenRouter 这些都有，Ollama 、LM Studio 、llama.cpp 、vLLM 一类的本地运行时也在。esc 随时取消，不会写入任何东西。 我日常挂的是 DeepSeek 。喜欢手动编辑配置的话，向 `~/.llm/config.json` 里写一个块就行 ```json { "providers": { "deepseek": { "kind": "openai-compat", "base_url": "https://api.deepseek.com", "api_key": "${DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}", "models": ["deepseek-chat", "deepseek-reasoner"] } } } ``` `kind` 只有两种，`openai-compat` 和 `anthropic`。`api_key` 可以直接写 key ，也可以写 `${环境变量名}`，请求的时候才去环境里读，key 不用落在配置文件里。同一个 provider 挂两个账号就 `/login` 两次，第二个会建议叫 `NAME-2`，之后模型用 `provider/model` 的完整 id 去挑，两边都提供的裸模型名会被当作歧义拒绝，而不是按顺序瞎猜一个。 模型在会话里用 `/model` 换，列表是实时拉的，你保存过的固定在最上面，`/thinking` 单独调思考深度。`-m` 和环境变量 `LLM_MODEL` 可以按次覆盖。 ## 基本用法 最短就三种 ```bash llm # 交互式会话 llm "fix the failing test" # 跑一个任务然后退出 cat error.log | llm "what broke?" # 提示词从管道来 ``` 管道输出是纯文本，没有颜色没有控制字符，直接重定向到文件或者接别的命令都行。 交互会话里该有的细节都有。任务跑着的时候随便打字，敲进去的内容会排队，在下一个工具调用的边界送达，相当于边跑边补充指示，一轮结束还没消费掉的自动变成你的下一条消息。ctrl+c 或者 esc 中断当前任务。`!cmd` 直接跑 shell 命令，tab 补全命令名和路径。ctrl+v 把剪贴板里的图片直接贴成附件，剪贴板里没有图片的话会告诉你它装的到底是什么。粘贴超过 10 行或者 1000 字符会折叠成一个原子 token ，提交的时候才展开，不会把输入框撑爆。 界面本身有一个刻意的决定，llm 不是 TUI 。codex 那类工具的交互是整屏接管的 alternate screen ，排版确实漂亮，代价是终端被它接管，输出不进 scrollback ，翻页搜索复制全是它自己实现的一套键位，退出之后屏幕恢复原样，刚才聊了什么全靠会话恢复找回来。llm 是普通的行式会话，回答逐行追加在终端的正常缓冲区里，回看历史用终端自己的滚动，搜索复制是终端原生功能，和你在 shell 里的肌肉记忆完全一致。渲染也是 write-once 的，回答区每个字节只写一次，不擦除不重绘，所以 kitty 、tmux 、纯 ssh 甚至串口控制台下面行为都一样。这类界面正经的名字是 REPL ，read-eval-print loop ，读一句执行一句打印一句再等下一句，psql 、sqlite3 、python 的交互模式都是这个形态，llm 的会话就是一个 chat REPL 。 附件也可以从命令行给 ```bash llm -a shot.png "what is wrong here?" llm -a https://example.com/page "summarise this" llm -a - "what is this?" /dev/null` 这种没事。 第二层是黑名单文件，值得展开讲讲。`~/.llm/blacklist` 对所有项目生效，`.llm/blacklist` 放在仓库根目录只对这个仓库生效，同名规则项目的行优先。这一层只能在硬拒绝之上做加法，你想放行某个硬拒绝是做不到的，硬拒绝就是硬拒绝。 文件首次生成时自带两条规则加一堆语法注释 ```text rm git push --force* ``` 删掉文件下次启动就重置回这两条。每行一个规则，写法有四种 ```text deploy # 命令词，拦 deploy x 、deploy --all 、echo hi | deploy git push --force origin main # 完整命令段，全部对上才拦 rm -* # glob ，拦 rm -rf 、rm -r ，但拦不住裸 rm !git push --force* # 反向放行，把前面对上的规则又放回来 ``` 匹配是对 shell 解析后的命令逐段做的，所以管道后面的段也能命中，`echo hi | deploy` 里 `deploy` 会被单独看到。`!` 开头的行用来在黑名单上开口子，比如全局拦了 `rm -*`，项目里写 `!rm -rf node_modules` 就把这一种放回来了。普通的 `rm` 默认不拦，删文件本来就是日常开发的一部分，真正危险的是 `rm -rf` 指错了地方，默认规则拦得比你想象中宽松，要严可以自己加 `rm -*`。 黑名单命中时会弹提示，高亮匹配到的那一行规则，可以看到到底是哪条规则拦住了你，按 `a` 在本次会话内放行这个模式，后续同模式的调用不再问。 要说诚实的话，这个检查是词法层面的，它看得到的是解析出来的命令段，看不到运行时才拼出来的东西，比如 `cmd="rm"; $cmd -rf /` 这种就不在它的视野里，扩展工具自己 spawn 的进程也不经过这条路。所以它是提示不是紧闭的牢笼，真要防护还是配合用户权限，拿日常账号跑 agent ，别拿 root 跑。 再细的控制写在 config.json 里，每个工具都可以单独给策略 ```json { "agent": { "tools": {"bash": "prompt", "git_push": "deny"} } } ``` `allow`、`deny`、`prompt` 三个值，双向都行，该问的问，该禁的禁，这一层的优先级最高。 ## 扩展系统 这是我最喜欢的设计。任何脚本开头加几行注释，它就变成了一个工具，host 每次调用的时候把它 spawn 起来，喂参数，收 stdout 作为结果 ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 # --- llm-tool: wordcount # description: count characters, words and lines of a text # args: text (string) the text to measure # arg-mode: argv # interpreter: python3 # timeout: 10 import sys text = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "" print(f"{len(text)} chars · {len(text.split())} words") ``` 不需要可执行权限，声明了 `interpreter` 就用指定的解释器跑，这一招在 Windows 上同样好使。Python 、shell 、R ，手边有什么就用什么写。只有一个参数的时候加一行 `arg-mode: argv`，参数就以普通命令行参数的形式进来，不用解析 JSON ，shell 脚本写起来毫无负担。文件放进 `~/.llm/extensions/` 是全局生效，放进项目的 `.llm/extensions/` 只对这个项目生效，两边同名的时候项目那份赢，改完 `/reload` 一下就挂上了。 更重的需求用常驻扩展。没有 manifest 头的文件按会话启动一次，通过 stdio 一行一个 JSON 和 host 通信。启动时 host 先发 `initialize`，扩展声明自己提供哪些工具、哪些斜杠命令、关心哪些事件，之后模型调用工具、用户敲命令、回合边界的时候 host 都会回调。整个协议可以用一小段 Python 讲完 ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 import json, sys def reply(obj): sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(obj) + "\n") sys.stdout.flush() for line in sys.stdin: req = json.loads(line) if req.get("type") == "initialize": reply({"id": req["id"], "result": {"tools": [ {"name": "deploy", "description": "Deploy the current tree", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}], "commands": [], "events": []}}) elif req.get("type") == "call_tool": import subprocess out = subprocess.run(["deploy.sh"], capture_output=True, text=True) reply({"id": req["id"], "result": out.stdout or out.stderr}) elif req.get("type") == "shutdown": break ``` 这就是一个完整的部署工具，核心一行都没改。扩展往 stderr 打的任何东西都是给人看的通道，调用进行中时会一行一行流进这次调用的工具日志，相当于长任务的实时进度，但是不会混进给模型的结果里。工具默认 120 秒超时，跑构建或者跑另一个 agent 这种长活在 `initialize` 里自己报一个更长的期限，上限一小时。扩展崩了会在下次用到的时候懒重启，代价是丢一次调用，不是丢整个会话。 事件里最有用的是 `tool_call`，它在每次工具真正执行之前触发，扩展可以拒绝这次调用，可以改写它的参数，也可以替它跳过审批提示。比如不想让 agent 在某个挂载了网络盘的目录里乱删东西，写一个几行的监听就拦住了，项目级的 guardrail 全靠这条缝，比任何模式开关都精准。`tool_result` 事件更进一步，能拿到工具的完整输出并改写模型实际读到的内容，日志去重、敏感信息脱敏都插在这里，线程文件里仍然保留原始输出，改坏了也赖不掉。 ## MCP MCP 没有做进内核，而是作为一个常驻扩展存在。`examples/extensions/mcp_bridge.py` 会读取放在自己旁边的 `mcp.json`，把里面每个 server 的工具挂载成 `server__tool` 形式的工具，审批矩阵照常适用。stdio 和 streamable HTTP 两种传输都支持，token 用 `${VAR}` 从环境变量展开，不用明文写进文件 ```json { "cloudflare": { "type": "streamable-http", "url": "https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp", "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer ${CLOUDFLARE_MCP_TOKEN}"} }, "fetch": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["mcp-server-fetch"]} } ``` 把文件拷进扩展目录，改一下旁边的 `mcp.json`，`/reload` 完事。一个 MCP server 握手失败就跳过它打个暗色警告，其余的照常挂载，不会因为一个坏 server 拖死整个会话。 ## subagent subagent 同样是扩展而不是内核特性。`examples/extensions/subagent.py` 挂载一个 `subagent` 工具，spawn 一个子 `llm` 进程，让它在自己的上下文窗口里干活，只把结论作为工具结果交回来。agent 的定义就是带 frontmatter 的 markdown 文件，放在 `~/.llm/agents/` 或者项目的 `.llm/agents/` 下面 ```markdown --- name: scout description: read-only scout that locates code and files tools: read, grep, glob, ls --- You are a scout. Locate code and report paths with brief evidence. Do not edit anything. ``` `tools`、`model`、`thinking` 都是可选的，正文就是附加的系统提示词。仓库里附了四个可以直接抄的定义，`scout` 和 `reviewer` 只读，`planner` 只思考不动手，`worker` 可以改文件可以跑命令。子进程通过 `--json` 输出事件流，扩展把它转成父会话里的实时工具日志，答案从最后的 `result` 对象里拿，完全不用解析面向人类的文本。ctrl+c 会沿着链路传下去把子进程也停掉，深度守卫拒绝套娃，子 agent 的工具白名单也不包含 `subagent` 自己。 核心对 subagent 的存在一无所知，这就是扩展系统该有的样子。 ## skills 和提示词模板 skills 放在 `~/.llm/skills/` 下面，一个目录一个 `SKILL.md`，`description` 是模型匹配任务的依据。agent 会在 `/help` 里列出所有可用的 skill ，可以 `/skill:name` 手动跑，模型看任务像的时候也会自己挑。运行的时候 skill 拿到自己所在目录作为工作目录，里面引用的 `references/`、`scripts/` 和各种资源在哪儿启动都能解析对。之前写过的生信项目梳理提示词，现在可以直接做成一个 skill ，每个项目目录里一敲就跑。 提示词模板解决另一个问题，就是反复敲同样的话。把一个 `.md` 文件放进 `~/.llm/commands/`，`/name` 就变成了一个斜杠命令，正文就是提示词，frontmatter 里可以加一个额外的 `system` 提示词，`$input` 接住命令名后面的所有参数，两边都会做替换。比如写一个 `review.md`，之后 `/review src/main.rs` 就是拿模板跑这个文件。 再往上一层是包管理。`llm install git:github.com/user/repo` 把一个 git 仓库克隆到 `~/.llm/pkg/` 下面，里面的 `extensions/`、`skills/`、`commands/` 会挂进正常的发现路径，`-l` 装到项目本地，`-g` 是默认的全局。仓库根上一个 `SKILL.md` 也算数，整个仓库变成一个 skill ，现在大多数独立 skill 仓库就是这个形状，直接装就能用。`llm list` 看每个包带了什么，`llm remove` 删掉。没有 npm 这条路，纯 git ，装之前自己审一遍，毕竟扩展是拿你的完整权限跑的。 ## 会话管理 每个会话都存成 `~/.llm/threads/` 下面的一个 JSONL 文件，模型、参数、每一轮的 token 用量、工具调用和结果全程在案，随时回来接着聊 ```bash llm -c "and in python?" # 接着最新的会话问，先看当前目录再全局找 llm -r # 浏览并恢复历史会话，可以边打字边过滤 llm --session 01ABC... "..." # 指定一个，短前缀就行 llm --fork "..." # 从当前会话分叉一条新的 llm --no-session "..." # 这次不存 llm export notes.md # 把会话导出成 markdown ``` 会话 id 是 ULID ，按时间有序。导出的 markdown 里工具调用和结果都在代码块里，思考过程收在专门的段落，系统提示词作为附录，attachments 按名字和类型记录而不是塞字节，直接能当文档归档。 ## 上下文和网络 上下文管理基本不用管，但管得很细。计费上下文超过窗口减 16384 的时候触发 compaction ，保留最近 20k token ，把丢掉的前缀总结成摘要，窗口大小未知的模型按 64k 走。如果请求发出去被 provider 告知超长，会立刻压缩再重试，不会让会话一次一次撞同一堵墙。`cache_ttl` 可以选 `5m` 或者 `1h`，长的那档写入计费贵一点，但是一次审批提示或者一轮长测试超过五分钟以后，下一轮就不用重写整个对话了，算下来是划算的。 网络层的细节都是踩坑换来的。重试带正负 10% 的抖动，退避从 1 秒到 30 秒，连接失败另有一套 5 秒到 60 秒的预算，服务器发了 `Retry-After` 就尊重它。流中途断了的话，已经产出的部分答案会保留成一条真正的消息接着续，而不是整轮丢掉重来，恢复次数上限五次。完全没有输出就断掉的请求原样重发，因为什么都没交出去，重发不会重复。300 秒没有任何输出的流按空闲错误处理，不让任务干挂在那里。请求体超过 32MB 会被本地拒绝，并且点名是哪些附件把它撑满的，`agent.max_request_bytes` 可以调低，网关在前面的时候经常比 provider 文档写的上限小得多。 代理走 `ALL_PROXY`、`HTTPS_PROXY`、`HTTP_PROXY` 和 `NO_PROXY`，自动生效，国内环境很实用。 ## 项目结构 代码组织按角色分层，一句话说清楚就是命令层薄，内核层厚，协议适配一层一个文件 ```text llm/ ├── src/ │ ├── commands/ # 子命令，一个文件一个，flags 、help 、接线 │ ├── core/ # 共享内核，配置、线程存储、http 、渲染 │ ├── providers/ # 协议适配器，openai-compat 和 anthropic 各一个，加共享消息模型和 provider 目录 │ ├── agent/ # agent 领域，循环、工具注册表、审批规则、扩展宿主 │ └── term/ # 终端领域，行编辑、选择器、spinner 、终端尺寸 ├── examples/ │ ├── extensions/ # 可运行的扩展，wordcount 、websearch 、mcp_bridge.py 、subagent.py 等 │ └── agents/ # 四个 subagent 定义，scout 、reviewer 、planner 、worker └── docs/ ├── architecture.md # 请求路径、agent 循环、工具注册表、扩展宿主、渲染契约 └── extensions.md # 插件接口，manifest 字段、每个消息和事件、tool_call 门、超时 ``` 这种分法的好处是改哪里都能立刻找到地方。加一个子命令就是往 `commands/` 里放一个新文件，接一个新协议就是往 `providers/` 里放一个适配器，agent 循环本身在 `agent/` 里，和终端呈现完全解耦，`--json` 模式下整个 `term/` 都不参与。测试全部内联在各模块的 `#[cfg(test)]` 里，就近看行为，单个跑用 `cargo test `。 扩展宿主也遵循同样的克制。host 负责 spawn 、stdio 、超时和尺寸上限，扩展自己声明工具、命令和事件，核心不认识任何一个具体扩展，MCP 桥和 subagent 都住在 `examples/` 里，和用户自己写的扩展没有地位差别，删掉它们核心照常编译。 想快速冒烟一下不改自己的状态 ```bash LLM_USER_PATH=/tmp/x cargo run -- "smoke test prompt" ``` ## 和 pi 的对比 写的过程中主要参照的对象是 [pi]( https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)，llm 的交互习惯和 compaction 规则都能看到它的影子，扩展协议也兼容 pi 的 API ，写好的工具命令钩子大部分能直接贴过来用。pi 本身做得很好，但它是 TypeScript 技术栈的，整个项目是一个 npm monorepo ，驮着 pi-ai 、pi-agent-core 、pi-tui 一大堆包，而我一直不喜欢 ts 技术栈的软件，所以动手用 Rust 重写了一个自己的，用下来 llm 比 pi 还快。 启动是最直接的差别。pi 背后是 Node.js 运行时，冷启动要过一遍 node 的初始化，而 llm 是 Rust 编译出来的单二进制，启动毫秒级，敲下回车会话就起来了，内存占用可以忽略，`grep` 大目录、`read` 分页读文件这些工具全是原生代码，没有一层 JS 转接，流式输出的每个字符直接写 tty ，长时间跑下来明显更安静。 依赖面的问题更实在。pi 装完带着一整个 node_modules ，为了供应链安全它官方文档里专门有一节讲依赖锁定，直接依赖全部固定精确版本，shrinkwrap 、npm audit 、生命周期脚本白名单一套全上，可见 ts 生态下这块有多让人操心。llm 这边 musl 静态链接，一个文件没有任何运行时依赖，根本不存在依赖链可被攻击的面，curl 一行装完，scp 到服务器 `chmod +x` 就能用，之前在曙光服务器上为了跑 agent 先装 node 再链 npm 的经历再也不需要了。 权限设计是理念上的分野。pi 不内置权限系统，文件、进程、网络、凭据全靠启动它的用户权限裸跑，官方的建议是需要隔离就拿容器或者沙箱包一层。llm 把这道墙做在了里面，硬拒绝加黑名单两层，提权、文件系统销毁、机器控制这些直接拦死，普通的日常操作又不打断你。我个人更信任后一种，容器隔离对大多数人是个不会去做的可选项，而内置的硬拒绝是每次都在场的事实。 功能上 llm 也做得更克制。pi 的功能基本都在主程序里，llm 把 MCP 、subagent 、websearch 这些全部拆成了扩展，核心只留八个内置工具，表面积小，能出错的地方就少。会话格式两边都是 JSONL ，llm 的 `--json` 事件流让子进程可以精确拿到每一轮的 token 用量，监督进程计费不用解析任何面向人类的文本，这一点在写 subagent 的时候特别舒服。 ## 和 codex 的对比 Rust 阵营里也试过 [codex]( https://github.com/openai/codex)，语言选对了，但功能上不太行。 最明显的是 provider 面窄。codex 是 OpenAI 自家产品，模型选择基本围绕自家接口转，第三方 provider 要靠 profile 手动配置 base_url 去兼容，配 DeepSeek 这类国产 API 能用，但体验明显是后妈养的，模型列表要手写，官方支持永远排在自家后面。llm 内置 38 个 provider 的接入配置，`/login` 选完就跑，`provider/model` 的命名一视同仁，谁也不比谁高贵。 扩展性是更大的差距。codex 没有插件系统，工具就那几个，想加个自己的工具要 fork 源码改 Rust 重新编译。llm 这边任何脚本加几行注释就是一个工具，常驻扩展能挂工具挂命令还能拦 tool_call ，MCP 和 subagent 都是这个机制长出来的，核心一个字节没改。这个差别日常用起来就是天壤之别，别人的工具再全，也不可能预判你项目里那个奇怪的需求。 会话管理也单薄。codex 的 resume 能找回上次对话，但没有 `--fork` 分叉、没有导出 markdown 、没有 `--json` 事件流给监督进程消费，会话就是会话，不是能被程序接续操作的数据。llm 的线程是纯 JSONL ，每轮带 token 用量，导出、分叉、被另一个 agent 当子进程驱动都是原生能力。 界面形态上也有一笔。codex 的交互是 ratatui 写的整屏 TUI ，好处是排版规整，代价是输出不进 scrollback ，翻页搜索得学它自己的键位，终端里其他工作流的习惯全不通用。llm 是行式的，会话就摊在正常缓冲区里，往上滚就是全部历史，管道接出去又是纯文本，同一个东西既是给人看的也是给程序读的。 然后是体感。codex 背靠大厂，启动要读配置要握手，比 pi 快但比 llm 慢，交互反馈也不如自己写的跟手，毕竟大项目的重心不在这科细节上。还有就是它绑定 OpenAI 生态的思路决定了它更像一个产品而不是一个工具，产品的功能边界由官方定义，工具的边界由使用者定义，我想要后者。 ## 测试情况 我主要在 Arch Linux 上测试，滚更很快，内核、终端、Wayland 环境一直在变，用下来没有任何问题。Kitty 和 Konsole 里交互会话、steering 、剪贴板贴图、斜杠命令都正常，fish 和 bash 下面管道和重定向也没有碰到过坑。 macOS 和 Windows 我手头没有长期使用的机器，prebuilt 目标都编译了，安装脚本也都在，但是设没设对只有真机知道。感兴趣的朋友可以帮忙测试一下这两个平台，碰到问题直接去 [GitHub Issues]( https://github.com/imjiaoyuan/llm/issues) 开一个，附上平台、终端和复现步骤就行。 ## 为什么自己写 之前在 [AI paradox](/074s9/) 那篇里写过，工具越顺手人越懒得思考。但一个自己写的 agent 恰好是解药，每一行为什么这么写、每个错误为什么这么报，我都清楚。模型请求失败了，我知道是重试预算用尽还是上下文超长，工具被拒了，我知道是硬拒绝、黑名单还是 per-tool 策略，扩展没挂上，`/status` 会告诉我原因。这种确定感用别人的黑盒工具是换不来的。 Rust 加 musl 的组合还顺手解决了部署问题，启动毫秒级，内存占用可以忽略，一个文件从最新的 Arch 到老掉牙的 CentOS 7 通吃，再也不用为了一台服务器单独折腾环境。 项目在 GitHub ，[imjiaoyuan/llm]( https://github.com/imjiaoyuan/llm)，MIT 协议，感兴趣的可以装一个玩玩，习惯终端工作流的人应该会觉得顺手。

projects.title: 放弃 Linear 后，我开发了 Gitstride：一个 GitHub Projects 的 macOS 原生客户端
projects.author: zwyyy456
projects.summary: 我之前半年，开发个人项目的时候一直在用 Linear 来进行项目管理。本来我以为免费配额是够用的，但最近几个月，我同时开发多个项目，Issue 就多了起来，Linear 的免费配额就不够用了，因此，我就转向了 GitHub Projects ，毕竟这些项目的代码本来就托管在 GitHub 上。 迁移到 GitHub Projects 之后，我发现它内置的 PR 与 Issue 联动工作流不如 Linear 完善，也不太符合我的需求。比如，当我给一个 Issue 关联 Draft PR 时，我希望这个 Issue 的状态能自动变成 `In Progress`；当 PR 准备好 Review 的时候，Issue 的状态也能跟着变成 `In review`。如果一个 Issue 关联了多个 PR ，我希望等这些 PR 全部合并之后，它才会进入 `Done`，而不是合并其中一个 PR 就算完成了。 此外，我也不太喜欢每次都要打开网页来管理项目，还是更想用本地客户端来操作。 所以，在 codex 的协助下，我用 Swift 6 开发了 [GitStride]( https://gitstride.hyperseek.tech/zh-cn)，一个 GitHub Projects 的 macOS 原生客户端。 GitStride 实现了前面提到的状态联动规则，我不用再随着 PR 的进度手动修改 Issue 状态。如果 Project 里没有 `In review` 这个状态，设置 GitStride 的 PR 自动化后，GitStride 默认会按需为你自动在 Project 中添加这个状态。 > 设置 PR 自动化时，也可以选择后续不追加 In review 这个状态。 GitStride 在菜单栏会常驻一个图标，点击图标可以快速查看项目 Issue ；等我真的要整理任务时，再打开主窗口，在看板或表格视图中创建和编辑 Issue 。 [![pn1KrPe.png]( https://s41.ax1x.com/2026/09/25/pn1KrPe.png)]( https://imgchr.com/i/pn1KrPe) [![pn1K2rt.png]( https://s41.ax1x.com/2026/09/25/pn1K2rt.png)]( https://imgchr.com/i/pn1K2rt) 为了确保创建 Issue 、更新 Issue 描述等需要向 Github 多次发送请求的操作的跟手，GitStride 开发时借鉴了 Linear 的 local-first 的理念。GitStride 会把项目快照缓存在本机。修改改状态后，界面会先显示变化，再同步到 GitHub ；创建或编辑 Issue 提交后，app 会马上显示新内容，后台处理向 Github 发起的请求。 GitStride 还支持创建 Backlog 状态的 Issue ，新建 Issue 时可以直接选择 Backlog 状态；如果 Project 里没有这个状态，GitStride 会自动补上。 项目已经[开源在 GitHub]( https://github.com/zwyyy456/GitBoard)。如果你也在用 GitHub Projects ，欢迎试试，如果觉得好用，还请给个 Star 。更多介绍，参见 [GitStride 官网]( https://gitstride.hyperseek.tech) 下一步计划 1. 添加命令面板功能、完善 app 内的快捷键操作 2. 添加甘特图视图

projects.title: Show HN: Whiteboard (YC W26) – An open-source IDE for thoughtful software design
projects.author: sidharthkmenon

github.name: devdotfast/whiteboard
github.description: open-source canvas for thoughtful software design

projects.summary: Hello! We’re Sid, Alex, Ketan, and Milan. We’re building Whiteboard ( https://whiteboard.dev.fast/ ), an open-source desktop app where humans and agents can architect software together in a common workspace. Here’s our repo: https://github.com/devdotfast/whiteboard . We were missing the feeling of a “whiteboard session” with another dev where you leave with a deep understanding of a system, so we built this app for ourselves. Whiteboard plugs into the tools you already use - e.g. Claude Code, Codex, etc. – and gives your agent an SDK to draw on an in-app canvas to describe its work. We began with an MVP based on HTML artifacts and started rethinking the app as we ran into limitations: 1. Built on top of CodeOSS: We found that in pure HTML tools it was hard to connect a spec or diagram to code. In Whiteboard, when you click on visualizations like a sequence diagram, an entity relationship diagram, or a quote from the agent’s trace, you can jump to the underlying code directly. When navigating code, you get keybindings and LSP support from VSCode out of the box. We’ve found this is especially valuable because tradeoffs are often only discovered after a first pass at implementation (re: slop) 2. Semantic diff viewer: we wrote a semantic, AST-aware diff viewer in Rust so you can only view the code changes which are relevant to you [1]. We’ve set up some sane defaults: large added functions are summarized as pseudocode, and things like unit tests and large documentation changes are collapsed / hidden. This is all customizable with a WASM-based plugin system. 3. Decision Log: We found it difficult to reason about what set of decisions our agents made autonomously. So we built tools for agents to query and link their own traces to the Whiteboard, so you can understand how the requirements that you set were implemented, and understand what decisions your agent made autonomously. Here’s a quick demo video explaining more: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ChPn3ftULWE Folks at companies like Salesforce and Modal are using Whiteboard today as a review tool for architecture or spec-level changes – really any change where they want to be involved: 1. Reviewing your own coding agent’s work: because Whiteboard makes it easier to review large amounts of code, folks will typically have their AI agents create a prototype and a corresponding Whiteboard session so they can iterate on the design. 2. Reviewing other people’s changes: We’ve found that Whiteboard is particularly helpful when composed with tools like Greptile. For example, you can run an automated code reviewer on small changes and escalate to a Whiteboard session for the changes that require human judgement. Why we built this: we’re four buddies from college who quit our jobs as tech leads right before agentic coding became industry standard. As we iterated towards an MVP for a previous idea, we struggled to maintain a comprehensible codebase while reaping all the velocity benefits of agentic coding. As more PRs were merged without our understanding, we felt a ‘cognitive debt’ begin to seep in, until it became difficult for us to even contribute to the system [2]. We’re releasing our desktop app under an MIT license. Please poke through and feel free to contribute! Eventually we’ll charge companies for a hosted web version that manages whiteboard session creation alongside features like trajectory storage and multiplayer reviews. Everything will always remain self-hostable. Thanks for reading, and we hope you try it out! We would love to hear any feedback and to learn from your expertise. Here’s are the project links again: https://github.com/devdotfast/whiteboard , and you can install (for MacOS + Linux) at https://install.dev.fast [1] diffs library: https://github.com/devdotfast/diffr [2] Credit for the term ‘cognitive debt’ goes to https://www.geoffreylitt.com/2026/07/02/understanding-is-the...

projects.author: 0x1062
projects.summary: Hey HN, I'm Jordan from Radix. Radix is a UI tool for programming agents. You prompt your agent to generate a workspace for a task you're working on and get an interactive widget that persists locally on disk. I built Radix because I always needed tools while I was writing code: tools to test little experiments, to play around with UI, to visualise results etc. Sometimes these would end up as python tools that read and plotted data, or separate React apps spun up just to test a single feature. Lately obviously I've been using Claude artifacts but these are quite limited. I wanted a system where it was easy to leave comments or adapt an artifact without having to give vague descriptions back to the agent, and where ideally I could actually shift away from a chat window as the main interface. I've got a pro version of Radix which I will launch soon. This current version is entirely free and is definitely a beta -- there will be rough edges! Note: There's no telemetry or data captured. Your messages run entirely through your own agent. I require a key but that's just to get an idea of how many people are using it. Everything is stored locally (the workspaces are actually just React apps which you can edit "artisanally" if you want). If you have any questions please reply here or email me hello@radix-os.com Thank you!

projects.title: Show HN: Critic – Review code with the agent that wrote it
projects.author: snyy
projects.summary: Hey HN, I'm Shreyash from Feyn. We help companies build custom models from their data. Today we're releasing Critic, a change review platform that lets you engage directly with the AI that wrote the code. Agents write most of our code. While that has made us more productive, understanding a change and its consequences has become incredibly difficult. As our company adopted more agentic tools, we found it harder to loop people in on the impact of a PR and the state of a project. We built Critic to fix this. Critic lets AI agents present their code, annotate key blocks, and include relevant evidence (like screenshots and instructions to run locally). Anyone viewing that change can talk directly to the agent that wrote it. See a demo here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U2--lytmOtQ . Critic works through a plugin for Codex or Claude Code. When your agent writes code, the plugin asks it to also write a narrative describing the story behind the change, and highlight any assumptions, decisions, or complex code. You can then view the change at critic.run or have your agent pull it via the bundled MCP. Every feature in Critic is available over MCP, so your agent gets all the same context without leaving its harness. From the dashboard or MCP, you can chat with the authoring agent directly. When Critic receives a question, it forks the authoring session and forwards your question there. That way your main thread stays clean and keeps working. Local changes are visible only to the owner. Anything pushed to GitHub is mirrored and visible to anyone with permission to view that change on GitHub. When building Critic, security was a big priority for us. AI agents often run in auto mode and can take many actions on your computer. We wanted to ensure that giving people access to your agent doesn't mean giving them access to your computer. All Critic forked sessions are stripped of their write tools. They can only answer questions about the change and in-progress work in that workspace. Critic has helped us catch several incidents before they hit production. The most common is a model not reusing artifacts, like existing styles, components, or functions. Because it's so easy to dig into an agent's work and question it, we've also caught more cases of models misdiagnosing issues or writing unhelpful code. Since Critic's UI is faster and friendlier to agents than GitHub, our team is returning feedback quicker as well. Critic is free to use. Sign up at https://critic.run . Let me know if you have feedback or questions.

projects.author: 1420079678-ctrl

github.name: 1420079678-ctrl/agent-body
github.description: Plugins as organs for DeepSeek Harness: nerve impulses route each command, a heartbeat circulates state, reflex arcs fire with zero model calls, sleep-time memory, closed-loop self-healing. Tool-schema gating cuts prompt tokens 84.7% (reproducible).

projects.summary: 这是一个 DeepSeek Harness 的插件框架，思路是把每个插件当成一个器官来写：插件只声明自己的能力、感知和反射弧，剩下的生理机能由内核补上——变速心跳、神经冲动路由、睡眠期记忆巩固、闭环自愈。缺一个器官不致命，会自动找能力重叠最高的器官代偿。 值得一说的是三处设计，数字都在仓库里可复现： 反射弧零模型调用。 确定性条件命中即毫秒级执行，不烧 token。更有意思的是它会自己长反射：同一个工具同一种失败重复三次，系统就写出一条反射弧，下次自动开火。开火五次零贡献的反射会被自动停用。 自愈是闭环。 失败先做确定性归因（工具缺失 / 参数错 / 权限 / 超时 / 网络 / 不存在 / 冲突），再按处方处置，而且要等那个器官下次真的成功了才算伤口闭合——不是修完就报成功。参数错误永不自动重试，因为重试只会放大错误。 装再多也不撑爆提示词。 工具 schema 按当前意图显影，仓库内冷启动基准：48 条代表性命令下省掉 84.71% 的 tool schema token，npm run bench:check 会在数字漂移时直接构建失败。这个项目本身就是在给「插件装多了提示词爆炸」这个真实痛点找解法。 不用装也能看它跑起来： sh git clone && cd agent-body npm run demo # 命令 → 冲动 → 支配 → 执行 → 归因 → 反射，离线、无密钥 npm run check # CI 门禁：常量表、目录、测试、基准，全部离线 已经装了 DeepSeek Harness 的话，一条命令装齐三个核心器官： sh dsh plugin --profile web add 1420079678-ctrl/agent-body 仓库是 monorepo，24 个插件包，其中 10 个另有一份可单独安装的 tarball。项目还在早期，文档和基准都在仓库里，欢迎拍砖。

projects.title: 放弃 Linear 后，我开发了 Gitstride：一个 GitHub Projects 的 macOS 原生客户端
projects.author: zwyyy456
projects.summary: 我之前半年，开发个人项目的时候一直在用 Linear 来进行项目管理。本来我以为免费配额是够用的，但最近几个月，我同时开发多个项目，Issue 就多了起来，Linear 的免费配额就不够用了，因此，我就转向了 GitHub Projects ，毕竟这些项目的代码本来就托管在 GitHub 上。 迁移到 GitHub Projects 之后，我发现它内置的 PR 与 Issue 联动工作流不如 Linear 完善，也不太符合我的需求。比如，当我给一个 Issue 关联 Draft PR 时，我希望这个 Issue 的状态能自动变成 `In Progress`；当 PR 准备好 Review 的时候，Issue 的状态也能跟着变成 `In review`。如果一个 Issue 关联了多个 PR ，我希望等这些 PR 全部合并之后，它才会进入 `Done`，而不是合并其中一个 PR 就算完成了。 此外，我也不太喜欢每次都要打开网页来管理项目，还是更想用本地客户端来操作。 所以，在 codex 的协助下，我用 Swift 6 开发了 [GitStride]( https://gitstride.hyperseek.tech/zh-cn)，一个 GitHub Projects 的 macOS 原生客户端。 GitStride 实现了前面提到的状态联动规则，我不用再随着 PR 的进度手动修改 Issue 状态。如果 Project 里没有 `In review` 这个状态，设置 GitStride 的 PR 自动化后，GitStride 默认会按需为你自动在 Project 中添加这个状态。 > 设置 PR 自动化时，也可以选择后续不追加 In review 这个状态。 GitStride 在菜单栏会常驻一个图标，点击图标可以快速查看项目 Issue ；等我真的要整理任务时，再打开主窗口，在看板或表格视图中创建和编辑 Issue 。 [![pn1KrPe.png]( https://s41.ax1x.com/2026/09/25/pn1KrPe.png)]( https://imgchr.com/i/pn1KrPe) [![pn1K2rt.png]( https://s41.ax1x.com/2026/09/25/pn1K2rt.png)]( https://imgchr.com/i/pn1K2rt) 为了确保创建 Issue 、更新 Issue 描述等需要向 Github 多次发送请求的操作的跟手，GitStride 开发时借鉴了 Linear 的 local-first 的理念。GitStride 会把项目快照缓存在本机。修改改状态后，界面会先显示变化，再同步到 GitHub ；创建或编辑 Issue 提交后，app 会马上显示新内容，后台处理向 Github 发起的请求。 GitStride 还支持创建 Backlog 状态的 Issue ，新建 Issue 时可以直接选择 Backlog 状态；如果 Project 里没有这个状态，GitStride 会自动补上。 项目已经[开源在 GitHub]( https://github.com/zwyyy456/GitBoard)。如果你也在用 GitHub Projects ，欢迎试试，如果觉得好用，还请给个 Star 。更多介绍，参见 [GitStride 官网]( https://gitstride.hyperseek.tech) 下一步计划 1. 添加命令面板功能、完善 app 内的快捷键操作 2. 添加甘特图视图

projects.summary: 大家好，自荐一个开源项目 Gear，希望帮助开发者提升 AI Agent 在具体任务中的表现。 开发 Agent 时，经常需要反复调整提示词、工具和执行流程，再跑一遍任务，检查改动是否有效。Gear 把这个过程组织成一个由评测反馈驱动的优化循环： 1. 准备一组有明确验收标准的任务，可以使用现有 benchmark，也可以定义自己的任务集。 2. 运行 Agent，收集执行轨迹和评测结果。 3. 由负责优化的 Agent 分析失败原因，修改授权范围内的组件。 4. 重新评测、比较候选版本，保留表现更好的方案，继续迭代。 可优化的组件包括提示词、工具实现、Skills、工作流和上下文管理。这些围绕模型的运行配置统称为 harness。Gear 会记录各版本的改动和评测结果，方便检查和复用；开发者也可以定制搜索算法，并根据通过率、费用或 token 消耗设置优化目标。 在项目公开的 AutomationBench Marketing 实验中，GPT 5.6 Luna + DSH 在 100 个公开任务上的任务通过率从 27% 提升到 53%，目标完成率从 75.37% 提升到 88.88%。这组结果包含 harness 优化和推理档位从 medium 到 max 的变化，且任务集参与过优化；实验配置与评分口径均已公开，便于读者判断结果的适用范围。 Gear 通过 Refine Skill 接入 Codex、Claude Code、DSH 等 Agent 环境。负责提出改进的 Agent 与执行任务的 Agent 可以使用不同模型。当前已支持 harness 优化，模型训练仍处于实验阶段。 项目采用 MIT 协议，提供中文文档和完整实验案例，欢迎试用、反馈和贡献。 GitHub 源码 中文文档与快速开始 实验过程与优化算法

projects.title: 【开源自荐】gcl2api-plus：支持多账号池、模型自动降级链与 Token 计费看板的 Gemini / Antigravity 转 API 网关
projects.author: Wzh0718

github.name: Wzh0718/gcl2api-plus
github.description: antigravity to api，并新增 多种新功能

projects.summary: 将 GeminiCLI 与 Antigravity 转换为兼容 OpenAI、Claude 和 Gemini 标准格式的自托管 API 网关。 基于上游开源项目二次开发，专注于生产与个人开发场景下的多账号池轮询调度、429 配额耗尽模型自动降级、API Key 权限分发以及 Token/费用统计监控。 为什么做这个项目？ 在使用各类客户端工具（如 Cherry Studio、NextChat、Cursor、各类 Agent 框架等）对接 Gemini 或 Antigravity 时，经常会遇到几个痛点： 1. 单账号配额易被限流：高频并发或重度使用容易触发 429 配额限制，单一模型一旦耗尽便导致调用链路全面中断。 2. 缺乏多凭证统一管理：手头有多个凭证时，手动切换繁琐，无法自动探测凭证失效（如 403 封禁）或健康状况。 3. 对外分发与用量失控：想要将接口分享给团队成员或部署到家庭服务器时，缺少独立的 API Key 权限控制与清晰的 Token 用量/费用账本。 因此本项目在转 API 的基础能力之上，重点补充了企业级/团队级网关所需的凭证健康生命周期管理与降级冗余机制。 核心特性 模型配额耗尽自动降级链：配置 ANTIGRAVITYMODELFALLBACKCHAIN 后，当高阶模型遇到明确的配额耗尽型 429 时，网关会自动平滑降级至备选模型（如 Flash / Tiered 版本），保障长任务或 Agent 链路不被阻断。 多账号凭证池与健康守护：支持多账号轮询调度、403 异常复核隔离、账号健康检查以及 RT / OAuth 一键登录管理。 完整的 API Key 与权限控制：支持签发独立 API Key，可单独设置权限范围、速率限制以及过期策略。 Token 用量与费用统计：内置可视化 Web 控制台，实时展示请求吞吐量、各模型 Token 消耗走势与费用账本。 高可用存储架构：以 SQLite 作为核心持久化主账本，可选配合 Redis 镜像加速计费统计与看板查询，支持非流响应大缓冲区与流式守护。 开箱即用：提供多架构 Docker 镜像（支持 amd64 / arm64），一条命令即可完成部署。 快速部署 使用 Docker 快速启动： bash docker run -d \ name gcli2api \ network host \ e APIPASSWORD=yourapipassword \ e PANELPASSWORD=yourpanelpassword \ e PORT=7861 \ v "$(pwd)/data/creds:/app/creds" \ ghcr.io/wzh0718/gcl2api-plus:latest 启动后访问 即可进入管理控制面板配置账号与模型降级链。 界面截图 | API Key 签发与权限管理 | 统计监控与费用账本 | | :---: | :---: | | | | | 账号与凭证管理 | 详细 Token 统计分布 | | :---: | :---: | | | |

projects.summary: 个人 AI 时代，现在这种 App 的形态还适应未来吗？像 Meta Muse 这样的云端 agent 就是终点吗？我们的答案是「会进化的 App 」。 **Mojito**（ MIT 开源）：在对话里说一句「把下一步放最上面，加粗」，跑在你自己 Mac 上的 Claude Code 就去改代码、构建、发布到手机 / Mac / 网页版，推送告诉你改了什么。 ![]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TimeLovercc/mojito/main/docs/media/hero-light.png) 三个原则： - **薄代码**：服务器上的 hub （ FastAPI + SQLite ）只存数据、提供 API 、发推送，功能不写死 - **agent 掌握上下文**：Claude Code 跑在你自己的 Mac 上，懂你的日程、邮件、文件，也懂这个 App 自己的代码和设计文档 - **和你一起进化**：小改动直接上线，大改动先等你点同意（目前由维护会话按文档判断，代码里还没强制） 一天里长出来的东西（真实记录）： - 「想要个订阅页」→ 订阅页 + 每个来源一键运行 - 「 iPhone 也要能用」→ 当晚就有了能加到桌面的网页版和 Web Push - 「通知收到两遍」→ 自己查到原因（安卓通知库自己又显示了一份）并修好 - 「桌面版像拉长的手机」→ 重做成 Mac 原生风格（新版还在开发） - 「加个英文界面」→ 中英切换 技术栈：Expo （ Android + PWA ）、Tauri （ Mac ）、FastAPI + SQLite 、Claude Code 。 实话实说：还是 alpha ，要自己部署（一台服务器或常开的电脑）；依赖 Claude Code ；数据在你自己的机器上，但 agent 读到的内容会发给你选的模型提供方。 GitHub： https://github.com/TimeLovercc/mojito 欢迎拍砖。独立项目，与 Meta 无关。

projects.title: Show HN: swe-mux – A terminal multiplexer for coding agents optimized for mobile
projects.author: jatora
projects.summary: I run a lot of coding agents at once, mostly Claude Code, Codex and pi, across several projects. I got tired of having so many windows open, of agents leaving hung processes behind, of tracking which one needed input, and of having to remote into my desktop or SSH into a single shell to manage them from my phone. Even then, a terminal on a phone couldn't show me the frontend or output I needed to verify the work. I tried Orca and herdr. Both were better than my setup, but neither had a real WYSIWYG markdown notes surface, and neither had a phone interface I could actually work in. swe-mux is the terminal multiplexer I built for that. It runs any shell or CLI in real terminals on your own machine and serves the same live sessions to your desktop and your phone. It's built around agents: Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi and oh-my-pi get a live status (working, done, or waiting on you), searchable history and resume. Anything else runs as an ordinary terminal with everything except the status. This is the actual terminal and not a UI wrapped around the agent, and you can just use it that way, or start claude in a plain shell and that pane becomes an agent session. On the desktop it's panes and tabs of sessions, notes, files and dev-server previews. Input behaves the same across agents: Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Backspace, paste and click-to-position work in all of them, shortcuts come from presets (tmux, VS Code, Vim, Emacs), and you can paste images straight from the clipboard. Notes and any markdown file in the project open in the same WYSIWYG editor, on desktop and phone, and autosave. No more scattered locations for notes. On the phone it's the same sessions over your own Tailscale network, installed as a PWA: the terminal with a usable keyboard, git diff review, files, notes, and push notifications when an agent needs a decision. A dev server on the host's 127.0.0.1 is proxied through swe-mux, so the phone can open it without exposing another port. Being able to play-test and check a frontend there is what finally closed the development loop on the phone for a lot of my projects. Now I can and do swe anywhere. It's a problem Two things I use constantly: a prompt queue, so something I think of mid-turn waits until the agent is done instead of interrupting it, and messaging between sessions, so a Codex session can ask a Claude session something. I don't want my workflow tied to one provider. General architecture: Sessions survive restarts. A separate supervisor process owns the terminals, so the daemon can restart and the app can update without killing anything. I update it several times a day, so this wasn't optional. Status comes from the CLI's hooks, its transcript and the terminal itself, because no single one reliably tells "waiting on you" apart from "busy in the background". There's no swe-mux account, no server of mine in the path, and no telemetry. Just your tailnet It was built on Windows, which is where I use it every day and the only platform with a packaged desktop app. The installer is unsigned, so the PyPI install is the way to avoid the SmartScreen prompt. macOS and Linux run the daemon and use a browser. CI runs it on all three, but I haven't lived on those myself, however Linux I have tested. Demo, the real UI with simulated agents, nothing to install: https://swemux.dev/demo/ Install: `uv tool install swe-mux` (or `pipx install swe-mux`), then run `swe-mux` on Windows or `swemux start` elsewhere. Apache-2.0: https://github.com/jatoran/swe-mux I've put a lot of work into the initial user experience to help streamline a quick setup depending on someone's needs, feedback greatly appreciated, thanks

projects.title: 集成 tailscale 的 android SSH/SFTP 终端
projects.author: netox
projects.summary: 之前分享过我的 iOS 应用 NovaScale(原名 NovaAccess), 它直接集成了 Tailscale 内核, 把 SSH/SFTP/Remote Codex 这些功能整合到一个 App 里, 无需开启 Tailscale VPN 客户端, 也可以在有 VPN 运行的情况下运行, 目前还在积极迭代基于 herdr remote 协议, 以满足像我这样重度 Tailscale 用户远程开发以及维护服务的一些需求 距离之前发贴已经有一段时间了，这期间 iOS 版本增加了很多新功能，同时也修复了一些 libtailscale 的问题(相关修复开源在 https://github.com/GalaxNet-Ltd/libtailscale 不知道为啥, 感觉 Tailscale 的 iOS 有些严重问题上游修复的不积极, 比如这个断网问题: https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/19504); 与此同时, 我也一直在用多余的 codex 额度(pro 5x 用户, 近期 reset 实在时太多了), 在开发一个全免费全开源的 Play 版本, 用来满足当时一些国内外用户提到的 android 版本需求 由于之前的一些方案感觉不理想, 在 5.6/astra 发布后又进了一些优化, 感觉逐渐达到了自己可用的情况, 甚至为 SSH terminal 增加基于 SGR 的鼠标支持(herdr 这种 mouse native 的 TUI 应用需要)基本上 Astra 一发就差不多了 最近重新把之前的 play 开发者账号用了起来, 全部委托给 codex 负责截图、描述、商店操作(甚至如何搞授权也是 codex 告诉我的, 相比 iOS 开发要复杂点), 没想到当前提交隔天就通过了 因此发在这里也分享给有需要的朋友, 提前声明如下: 1 、这是一个完全免费的应用，代码完全开源 ( https://github.com/GalaxNet-Ltd/novascale-android), 与 iOS 版本不同, 没有采用 libtailscale, 直接让 codex 基于 tailscale 源码适配 2 、半年前的最初版本大概还是 claude 做的, 感觉做的不怎么样, 当前完全由 Codex 开发, 我只负责架构文档和最终的验收, 所以可以称之外完全 AI 开发并发布的版本, 后面可能会根据用户反馈、时间和 Codex 额外会进行一些迭代; 总体上感觉满足我有时候 iPhone 没电时用 Android 手机的需求 3 、代码为 GPL 协议, 原因在于从 termux 上借了一些 terminal rendering 的代码, 这部分它的协议是 GPL 的, 因此也只能 GPL 开源 Android 版本 NovaScale 的一些主要功能如下: - 无需安装 Tailscale 官方 App ，因此可以同时使用其他 VPN - 基于 libghostty(准确说是 libghostty-vt 库) + Termux 渲染方案 - 支持鼠标操作（因此 tmux / herdr 等场景可以正常使用） - 支持剪贴板功能（包括 OSC52 ） - 支持自定义控制服务器(即支持 headscale 或其他自建 tailscale coordinator) - 内置 SFTP 文件浏览器，支持直接编辑文件, 以及少量代码类型的高度支持 - 内置浏览器，可访问 tailnet 内部的 Web 服务 - 支持后台代理，让第三方应用使用 tailnet 连接, 例如你正在使用其他非 Tailscale VPN 时，也可以配合 Termius 等 SSH 客户端连接服务器 技术架构如下: - tailscale 源码包装出 lib - russh 通过 ffi 与 tailscale lib 进行通信, 实现 ssh 通道 - 使用 termux 提供的代码实现了一个 terminal UI 的渲染 - tailscale lib 中提供一个 socks5 代理, 此代理供浏览器实现基于 MagicDNS 的访问, 同时这个代理可以提供给其他进程使用 如果你是 Android 用户，并且对此感兴趣，可以通过如下链接下载: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=cc.galaxnet.novascale 简单推广下 iOS 版 NovaScale ，它包含 Android 版的全部功能，基础功能免费, 有少量的付费功能需要订阅或买断支持: - 多 tailnet 支持 - 基于内置 Tailscale 和主机 Codex App-Server 直接交互的远程 Codex 方案(无需第三方中转) - 服务器监控 - Docker 管理 目前我还在尝试通过 herdr 的协议实现原生 herdr 支持，让它能够像 herdr remote 一样工作。 iOS 版本可通过如下链接下载: https://apps.apple.com/cn/app/novascale-%E4%B8%93%E4%B8%BA-tailscale-%E6%89%93%E9%80%A0/id6749938291 PS: 1 、最近看到 tailscale CEO 也忍不住充了点 codex 的额度, vibe 了一个内置 Tailscale 的 jellyfin 客户端, 同样也是基于 libtailscale 实现的, 有需要用户可以去他的 X 的帖子上翻翻应该能找到 testflight 2 、作为 tailscale 的重度用户, 也欢迎私信技术交流

projects.title: 世界首款基于 jev 的 AI 实时模拟小镇上线了，比斯坦福小镇 200 倍速度，成本减少 90%！
projects.author: Koimiao

github.name: NevaMind-AI/JevTown
github.description: jev based AI town simulation

projects.summary: 最近 jev 的讨论挺多，我们把它接进了「斯坦福小镇」的 agent 模拟世界，做了一个小实验。 虽然它用了像素风游戏的表现形式，但这个世界里没有玩家角色。人类只能观察，不能控制居民。画面中所有会移动的角色，都是 agent 依靠 jev 自己决定要去哪里、找谁，以及什么时候停下来。 目前场景里有 20 个居民。每个人都有自己的身份、性格、当前状态和对世界的共同认知。 世界运行后，他们会不断经历这样一个循环： 观察当前环境 → 决定下一步做什么 → 移动 → 发起互动 → 对话 → 更新状态和记忆 这次主要实验的是：能不能让 jev 来负责 agent 最频繁的「下一步做什么」决策（ repo 里面有录屏） 我们的做法不是让模型自由生成一段 JSON ，而是先由引擎计算出当前合法的候选动作，例如： - 现在可以接近哪些人或物体 - 可以走向哪些地点 - 是否值得主动接触某个目标 - 如果不行动，应该短暂停留还是等待更久 然后把这些候选项交给 Jev 。一次请求里会同时询问 seek 、target 、roam 、place 和 idle_length ，再由代码按照固定规则组合成最终动作。 这样做主要解决了一个之前比较麻烦的问题：普通对话模型即使被要求输出 JSON ，仍然可能选择一个根本不存在、或者当前不可达的目标。Jev 的 Choice 问题只能从引擎提供的候选项里选择，相当于让非法动作从结构上就无法被表达。 同时，它还会返回每个选项的概率和置信度，所以右侧观察面板里可以看到类似这样的记录： seek 0.83 · talk to Ovid p=0.62 c=0.70 这比让模型事后生成一句“我为什么这么做”，更方便观察 Agent 的真实决策过程。 当然，Jev 目前并没有负责整个 Agent 。 它只替换了动作决策这一环。人物对话、长期状态描述和记忆仍然由对话模型与 Embedding 完成。Jev 不生成文本，所以它很适合从有限选项中快速做决定，但不适合直接承担人物对白。 技术上目前是 TypeScript + React + PixiJS 。模拟本身运行在浏览器中，Node 代理只负责保存模型凭证和转发请求。默认运行 20 个 agent ，也可以调整到 50 个，用来观察多人场景下的行为和调用压力。 当前版本还有不少限制： - 只有一个主要观察场景 - 默认刷新页面会重新开始一个世界 - Agent 数量增加后，对话模型的调用成本仍然比较明显 - Jev 不生成 intent 和动作描述，人物接近目标后的行为有时会显得比较直接 - 这仍然是一个 Agent loop 的实验，不是完整的虚拟社会 这里说的「斯坦福小镇」，主要指 Generative Agents / Smallville 这一类“观察数字居民自主生活”的方向，并不是对原项目的完整复刻。项目的早期工程基础来自 a16z 的 AI Town ，我们在上面继续做了自己的世界、像素场景和决策层实验。 代码和运行方式放在这里： https://github.com/NevaMind-AI/jev-town

github.description: Keep Claude Code working through usage limits: exact reset times, handoff before the limit, headless runs that resume after the reset. MIT.

projects.summary: （MIT） 主页： 它解决什么 用 Claude Code 的 Pro/Max 订阅跑长任务时，5 小时或每周额度一到，正在跑的子 Agent 会一起失败；额度重置后主 Agent 通常把同样的任务从头重新派发，之前做的一半活作废，额度再花一次。我翻了自己 6 个会话的记录：449 个子 Agent 被限额打断，只有 8 个被按 ID 叫醒（而且都是在重置前叫的，所以又失败一次），438 个重做。 其实 Claude Code 已经把需要的信息写在本机了：transcript 里有精确的重置时间（quotaLimits.resetsAt），状态栏会收到 5 小时/7 天的用量百分比，每个子 Agent 的记录里有它的任务、改过的文件和最后几步。agent-limit-retry 只是把这些读出来，在正确的时刻告诉 Agent 该做什么。 它做什么 npx agent-limit-retry 一条命令安装：装 Claude Code 插件，接上状态栏（已有状态栏会保留并透传） 额度用到 90% 时，让 Agent 做完当前一步先写 HANDOFF.md（目标、已完成、进行中、下一步、坑），每个窗口只提醒一次 撞限额时记下精确的重置时间，发桌面通知 alr run "<任务>"：无人值守跑 claude -p，撞限额后睡到重置时间，用 --resume 续跑同一个会话，周限额同样处理 alr selftest：本地假接口模拟一次撞限额 + 自动续跑，不花额度 alr status：看两个窗口的用量和重置时间 全部在本机运行：不走代理、不需要账号、不联网、不轮换账号，只帮你把已经付费的套餐用干净。子 Agent 按原 ID 续跑那部分（Claude Code / Codex / ZCode 都支持）是付费的 Pro 版，基础功能开源 MIT。 Node.js 18+，Claude Code 2.1.234+。英文界面，中文 locale 下自动显示中文。

projects.title: Show HN: Ax – Let Claude, Codex and OpenCode talk to each other locally
projects.author: rcdexta
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m RC. When I worked at ThoughtWorks, we were pretty religious about pair programming: one person driving, another reviewing, both working through the same problem. Most of us have already paired with an agent in our own coding sessions. Some of us have even tried putting agents in both seats: one implementing, the other reviewing. I really like Claude Code’s cross-session messaging. I wanted that same experience between Claude, Codex, and OpenCode. The existing setups meant installing a new app or plugins that just don't work reliably. I wanted something local that stayed out of the way, let me keep using each tool as usual, but enabled hetergenous messaging. That became Agent Exchange, or ax. After installing, start two sessions in separate terminals: ax claude -n api ax codex -n web Then ask Codex: “Ask api whether the schema is ready.” The agents address each other by name, and replies come back into their conversations, including across repositories on the same machine under the same OS user. You can also connect existing conversations using each tool’s native resume syntax. AX supports Claude Code, Codex CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, and Pi. Underneath, it’s a local Go broker, Unix sockets, and a SQLite mailbox. There’s no AX cloud relay or telemetry. The messaging runs locally; the coding agents still communicate with their configured AI providers. We’ve been using it to send AX’s own PRs between Codex and Grok for review. I’d be interested in which agent combinations you use, and what you currently have to relay between them yourself.

projects.title: Show HN: Yengi, a local-first AIdevelopment environment for coding,Blender/Unity
projects.author: mdaiWorks
projects.summary: I've been working on Yengi for several months. I am a teacher, not a professional software developer. My path here started with Microsoft Small Basic, Scratch, and MIT App Inventor, which I used to teach children. I originally started it for a simple reason: I was using VS Code + Copilot, Trae, Cursor and Google Antigravity, and I kept running into usage limits and provider-specific workflows. I wanted something where I could choose my own model or API, including local models running through Ollama, and build without being tied to one provider. It grew considerably beyond that original idea. Yengi is a .NET 10 / WPF desktop application with: * Agent and tool system for files, terminal, Git, builds and tests * RAG and LSP integration * Verification loops with checkpoints and rollback * 30+ agent tools * Support for local models and external APIs * A custom 1.5B router model that I fine-tuned on thousands of examples of Yengi-specific agent decisions * 200+ automated tests It also has three additional modes besides the coding environment: *Blender:* Yengi can communicate with Blender, generate `bpy` scripts, keep conversational scene context, and optionally inspect Blender viewport screenshots through a multimodal model. I also added an optional prompt-engineering layer. For example, "create a low-poly tree" is expanded into a more detailed 3D-oriented instruction before being sent to the model. A follow-up such as "add five red apples to this tree" can modify the existing scene rather than starting from scratch. *Unity:* Yengi can work with Unity projects, generate C# components and interact with the Unity Editor. *Image generation:* Images can be generated from the development environment and saved directly into the project. The unusual part is how I built it. I used AI coding tools heavily, particularly Google Antigravity and GitHub Copilot. I didn't manually type the majority of the C# code. My role was primarily architecture, agent behavior, security boundaries, verification and rollback logic, router training, testing, debugging AI-generated changes, and integrating the different systems. I'm still trying to figure out how much of this approach is genuinely useful and how much is me having fun building increasingly complicated things. The project is free and open source under AGPL-3.0: https://github.com/mdaiWorks/yengi I'd especially like feedback from people working with .NET/C#, coding agents, local models, Blender or Unity. In particular, I'm curious about: * Is a small fine-tuned local router actually useful for this kind of agent? * Does the verification/rollback architecture make sense? * Are the Blender/Unity integrations useful beyond being demos? * If you were building this, what would you simplify or change? I'm not trying to claim that this replaces VS Code or Cursor. I'm interested in whether this particular approach is useful at all, and what I should change next.

projects.title: Show HN: OpenAPPA – open-source deterministic guardrails that don't break agents
projects.author: motakuk
projects.summary: Hi Hacker News! Matvey, one of the authors, is here. While building enterprise agents, we ran into a problem: the more tools you connect to the AI, the higher the chance it will run out of control and leak sensitive data. Guardrails, in theory, should prevent this, but the situation is worrying: - Non-deterministic guardrails (LLM as a judge, auto modes, etc.) are vulnerable to prompt injections, or they lack knowledge of the data, making them inefficient (~10% data leaks on our benchmarks). - Existing deterministic guardrails (Cedar, OPA, FIDES, Dogwood) require massive case-specific IF-ELSE-like policies and break agents (~59% utility loss on our benchmarks). We did something differently. We’ve taken the best of existing deterministic guardrails and built a policy language that is data-specific, not use-case specific. It lets you scale agents without updating a policy. On top of that, we’ve added multiple tricks (like a remedy plan or a DualLLM pattern) to help agents operate within those restrictions, raising utility from ~40% to ~90% and making it the first deterministic guardrail that doesn't break agents. Finally, we’ve designed it to be pluggable into any agent loop with pre- and post-tool-call hooks. We invite you to check out our benchmarks: https://www.openappa.com/evaluation Play with it in Claude Code: https://www.openappa.com/claude-code Try plugging it into your agent: https://www.openappa.com/add-to-agent Or check the academic paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24625 We'd love to hear any feedback!

projects.title: Show HN: I emulated Roborock's cloud so my vacuum works without internet
projects.author: Lash-L
projects.summary: Hi! I maintain the python-roborock library and the Roborock integration in Home Assistant. Roborock vacuums use a local protocol for direct commands, but they still route all map data strictly through the cloud (even though the map is stored locally). Even worse, if you try to block the vacuum from accessing the internet on your router, it will constantly reboot its Wi-Fi connection trying to re-establish a cloud connection, meaning you can't rely on just using a private local connection. I built a self-hostable version of Roborock's cloud: https://github.com/Python-roborock/local_roborock_server It works without having to open the device or root it, taking advantage of a couple of quirks during the onboarding process: 1) The vacuum has api-%s.roborock.com baked into its firmware. It injects the region directly into the string and this is the first exploit we take advantage of. The app will send in your region as a two letter code, e.g. 'us', 'eu', 'cn'. We send in a full URL ending with a '/' (e.g. 'example.com/'). The vacuum then treats "api-example.com" as the host and the rest as the URL path(e.g. 'api-example.com/.roborock.com'), directing its traffic to your server so long as there is a valid HTTPS certificate on that domain. 2) The second part of the handshake requires encrypting a message via a public key that is stored on Roborock's cloud where the private key pair is on the vacuum. We are able to reverse engineer the public key as the robot sends signatures with its message. Because of how RSA works, each signature is mathematically tied to the secret public key plus some extra noise. By gathering a few signatures across multiple onboarding attempts and taking their greatest common divisor, the noise cancels out and cleanly isolates the vacuum's actual public key which allows the server to encrypt its response and complete the pairing. I have a full technical write up here: https://python-roborock.github.io/local_roborock_server/tech... I wanted to share this on HN as I think this points to a very interesting thing that is happening. I have been playing with this idea for years in my head and I have not been able to get it to work (and I am not the only one who had looked into the api-%s avenue). I'm not a cryptography expert and had no idea that the signature exploit was even possible. I was stuck for long enough that I decided to throw the problem at some long-running agents, and they found the greatest common divisor exploit. IoT companies put most of their security effort into the cloud, since that's what they actually run. The vacuum is just one device on someone's home network, so it gets less attention and corners get cut. I think LLMs that are willing to throw themselves at a problem for hours are going to make stuff like this a lot easier to pull off and a lot more common.

projects.summary: 自荐一个最近做的开源项目 GitScry - 你的git历史就是一座藏宝库。 GitScry 是一个用 Rust 编写的命令行工具。它希望解决一个问题：很多对开发很有价值的信息，其实已经存在于 Git 历史里，但通常需要手动组合 git log、git blame、旧 diff、revert 记录和文件历史才能找到。 GitScry 会把这些历史整理成可以直接查询的问题，例如： 以前有没有实现过类似的改动？ 某一行代码或某个 symbol 为什么会存在？ 哪些文件历史上经常一起修改？ 修改这个文件时，通常还需要看哪些测试？ 某种方案以前是否尝试过，后来又被放弃或 revert？ 哪个 commit 可能引入了当前 regression？ 已知一个 bug fix，最初引入这段错误代码的是哪个改动？ 一些特点 完全基于本地 Git history，Git 仍然是 source of truth 本地建立可重建缓存，不需要上传代码，你的藏宝库永远属于你自己 查询结果会保留对应的 commit、path、confidence 和 evidence 支持 Linux、macOS 和 Windows 人类与 agent 均可以使用 目前已经在 git/git、curl/curl、rust-lang/rust、NousResearch/hermes-agent 等真实仓库历史上测试过不同查询，README 里放了一些 benchmark 和实际示例。 项目目前还在早期阶段，欢迎使用和反馈。

projects.summary: 很多项目 CI 一路全绿，不是因为代码没问题，而是那条检查规则从来没真正生效过。greencheck 会在你的配置和代码里自动制造小改动：删掉一行、把数值改成 0、清空一个字段，然后看你的门禁还拦不拦得住。拦不住的地方，就是它根本没在管的地方。纯 Python 标准库实现，零第三方依赖，装完直接用，不用改你现有的门禁配置。 亮点 1. 审计的对象是「门禁本身」而不是被检查的代码。同类工具大多在查代码，查检查规则的很少。 2. 零依赖、pip install 完就能跑，也可以直接 python -m greencheck.cli 调用，不侵入现有 CI。 3. 示例自带、可复现：仓库里的 demo 会当场跑出一个逃逸的变异——把 "replicas": 3 改成 0（一个永远起不来的服务），而门禁只说「键都在、值都非空」，所以放行。结构上的每条规则都还成立，这正是这类缺口能活下来的原因。 4. 不夸大：输出明确写着「这些是值得你去想的问题，不是结论」，不会拿变异数冒充缺陷数。 5. 同一个思路还能用来审计指标：一个永远等于 1.0 的自评分，不是测量出来的，是装饰。

projects.summary: AI agent 说它做完了，你现在只有两个选择：信它，或者自己把 diff 重看一遍。precheck 给第三个选项。它做两件测试框架不会做的事：第一，验收检查必须在动工之前写好并被哈希锁死，所以干活的那一方没法把考试题目改成自己会的；事后改一个字，之前所有结论全部作废——这是可验证的，不是靠约定。第二，检查通过之后，它会把被检查的产物改坏再跑一遍；在坏输入上照样通过的检查，从来就不是证据。 亮点 1. 审计的对象是「证明本身」。pytest 问的是「代码对不对」，precheck 问的是「你的证明对不对」——后者目前几乎没有工具。 2. 预注册是机制不是口号：检查在开工前冻结入哈希链，precheck verify 一条命令就能查出事后改动、删条目、跳序号。任何人拿到仓库都能自己验，不需要信任你。 3. 变异审计带具体改动：4 种变异（删行 / 置空 / 改数 / 截断）确定性地改坏产物再跑，逃逸的检查逐条列出改成了什么，比如 replicas: 3 -> 0 —— 一个永远起不来的服务，检查照样说通过。 4. 零依赖纯标准库、不联网、不侵入现有 CI；19 个单测；Linux / Windows / macOS × Python 3.8–3.13 全绿（9/9）。自带 composite GitHub Action。 5. 不夸大：输出明确写着「这是问题列表，不是 bug 列表」，README 有独立的 Limits 段落讲清它证明不了什么——包括「哈希链只能证明历史没被事后改动，不能证明第一条记录是诚实的」。

projects.title: Show HN: Ox – A local agent that uses the internet for you
projects.author: ziyzhu
projects.summary: I’ve been building Ox, a local, open-source agent that uses the internet for you. Ox acts as an intelligent proxy between you and the internet. It uses websites and apps on your behalf, freeing you from attention-hungry interfaces and slow legacy services. As it works, it can turn what it learns into reusable actions (basically function calls), making future interactions deterministic and way faster. Most service integrations today are still built ahead of time: someone writes an API integration, connector, MCP server, or browser automation and then maintains it as the service changes. But the internet is becoming more dynamic so have our agents. With Ox, instead of waiting for a connector, you can say something like: “Connect to <service>.” Ox can study a website or workflow through capabilities it already has, turn what it learns into typed actions and reusable skills, validate them, and make them available immediately. That pushed me toward local agents. A local agent operates from your own device, network, and existing authenticated browser sessions instead of relying on shared datacenter infrastructure. This also makes it less likely to hit blocks aimed at datacenter IPs or centralized browser automation. The model doesn’t need your passwords, cookies, or session tokens. Authentication and browser state are owned by the Host, while the agent interacts through explicit actions that could be gated. Ox is completely free and open source. You can use any model provider, including local or self-hosted models, while keeping your agent’s data on device. As local models improve, I think this architecture becomes increasingly useful because the agent can become more capable without requiring more of your data to leave your device. The security model is also a big part of the design. Ox asks before taking sensitive actions, keeps credentials isolated from the model, limits what agent code can access, and lets you stop execution at any time. Underneath the app is OpenOx, an open protocol for self-evolving agents. It separates the interface, agent, model provider, persistent state, execution environment, and external capabilities. The agent can run JavaScript inside a capability-limited VM. The VM has no direct network access, Host filesystem access, shell, Node.js, or DOM. Anything outside the VM has to go through an explicit ox.* capability exposed by the Host. Services provide typed actions for websites, device capabilities, or MCP servers. Skills provide reusable instructions for combining those actions. New services and skills can be attached at runtime without waiting for a new version of the app. They can remain local or be recorded in Git and shared through repositories, so each Ox can evolve independently while benefiting from capabilities learned by others. The agent’s persistent state lives in a portable Ox Profile containing its identity, memory, skills, artifacts, and conversations. The goal is for that state to stay independent of any particular interface, including Ox itself, or model provider. File over app. The first implementation is an iOS app. It’s available on the App Store, and the whole thing is open source: https://openox.ai/ https://github.com/ziyzhu/openox If you’re interested in the broader motivation behind the project, I wrote about it here: https://ziyzhu.com/a-technology-for-free-will This is still early. I’m especially interested in feedback on the security model and self-evolution. I built Ox from scratch but many aspects of the project were heavily inspired by Pi/OpenClaw and the idea of malleable software. Ox’s core agent loop on iOS is pretty much a Swift rewrite of the Pi core package. Happy to answer anything about the implementation or protocol.
